papers.title: PoKER: A Probability of Kill Estimation Rate Model for Air-to-Air Missiles Using Machine Learning on Stochastic Targets
papers.summary: This work introduces PoKER, a novel probabilistic model engineered to optimize missile launch effectiveness in air-to-air scenarios, specifically within Beyond Visual Range (BVR) air combat. Unlike conventional Weapon Engagement Zone (WEZ) models that delineate zones based on static distances such as maximum, minimum, and no-escape ranges, PoKER applies machine learning to predict kill probabilities more accurately by integrating the stochastic behaviors of targets and missile miss distances. This model dynamically evaluates target behavior, greatly expanding the predictive capabilities of engagement analysis. By factoring in elements such as warhead lethality, target and shooter orientations, and the specific conditions of engagement, PoKER provides important insights into engagement dynamics and quantifies success probabilities. Consequently, it can potentially be an important tool for BVR air combat pilots, improving operational decision-making within this specialized combat domain.
papers.comment: Accepted manuscript. 18 pages, 10 figures, 5 tables. Code available at https://github.com/jpadantas/poker
papers.journal: The Journal of Defense Modeling and Simulation: Applications, Methodology, Technology (2025)

papers.title: A Foundation Model for Policy In-Context Longitudinal Causal Effect Estimation
papers.summary: Longitudinal causal effect estimation is complicated by time-varying confounding and treatment-confounder feedback loops. Existing methods generally require data-specific nuisance-model fitting, and many are tailored to prespecified treatment sequences or prediction horizons, leading to time-consuming computation at deployment. We introduce *Policy In-Context Longitudinal causal Effect estimation with Prior-data Fitted Networks* (**PICLE-PFN**), the first foundation model for longitudinal causal effect estimation that supports *dynamic* treatment policies. PICLE-PFN represents target policies through in-context history-decision demonstrations, providing a unified interface for a broad class of treatment policies. Pretrained over synthetic data sampled from longitudinal structural causal models, PICLE-PFN amortizes causal effect estimation across datasets, policies, and horizons. Given a new observational dataset and target policy, it directly predicts conditional average potential outcomes (CAPOs) in one forward pass without task-specific training or hyperparameter tuning. Across synthetic and semi-synthetic longitudinal benchmarks, PICLE-PFN achieves competitive RMSE and substantially improved uncertainty calibration with a fraction of deployment runtime, compared to state-of-the-art conventional estimators trained and tuned separately for each dataset.

papers.title: Trust-Region Benders for Scalable Multiperiod Expansion Planning for Transmission and Storage
papers.summary: Transmission expansion planning (TEP) seeks to identify cost-effective investment strategies that enable power systems to reliably meet future demand, while accounting for the location, timing, and operational impacts of infrastructure upgrades. As demand grows and renewable penetration increases, there is growing interest in jointly modeling energy storage investments to enhance operational flexibility. This work presents a multiperiod formulation that co-optimizes transmission reconductoring and energy storage installation across multiple planning periods. To solve the resulting large-scale problem efficiently, a Benders decomposition with per-period trust-region stabilization and a relaxation-based warm-start procedure is proposed. The approach is demonstrated on a 2,000-bus Texas system, producing an investment plan spanning 2030-2045 with optimality gap below 1.0%, and is compared against a rolling-horizon approach to highlight the benefits of multiperiod coordination.
papers.comment: Presented at PowerUp 2026, September 9-11, 2026, Boulder, Colorado

papers.title: GRB 260924A: Extreme Energetics, Bright GeV Emission, and Exceptional X-ray and Optical Luminosity
papers.summary: We present a multiwavelength study of GRB~260924A at $z=3.51\pm0.10$ using \textit{Fermi}, \textit{Swift}, and ground-based optical and near-infrared observations. Its isotropic-equivalent gamma-ray energy, $E_{γ,\mathrm{iso}}\simeq9.79\times10^{54}$~erg, places it among the most energetic GRBs observed. The prompt emission comprised two bright episodes separated by weaker activity. The X-ray afterglow ranked among the most luminous in our comparison sample at selected post-flare epochs, with a luminosity comparable to that of GRB~221009A at a rest-frame time of 3.5~ks. At a common redshift of $z=1$, the optical afterglow outshone GRB~221009A by approximately 2~mag at 0.3~d and 1~mag near 1~d. LAT emission extended to approximately 1100~s and showed an early excess above the subsequent decay. The highest-energy photon, 43.3~GeV, arrived at 82~s during the first episode; a 14.2~GeV photon arrived at 304~s between episodes. We describe the afterglow light curves through forward-shock synchrotron and synchrotron self-Compton (SSC) emission, with reverse-shock SSC accounting for the early LAT excess. We connect the early and late afterglow phases by modelling the X-ray rebrightening at several kiloseconds through energy injection from trailing ejecta and evolving shock microphysics. The late afterglow suggests a stratified medium, modelled as $n(R)\propto R^{-1.2}$. Within this interpretation, the magnetic contrast $R_B\equiv(\varepsilon_{B,r}/\varepsilon_{B,f})^{1/2} \simeq2.6$ suggests magnetized ejecta, while the highest-energy LAT photons exceed the predicted synchrotron limit, supporting an SSC contribution.

papers.title: Near-critical Ising interfaces in the thermal direction: Absolute continuity with respect to SLE$_3$
papers.summary: The scaling limits of interfaces in the critical two-dimensional Ising model are described by the Schramm--Loewner evolution $\mathrm{SLE}_3$. While, in the scaling limit, the law of the whole near-critical FK-Ising configuration is known to be singular with respect to the critical law in the thermal direction, and the same is expected for the spin configuration, we prove in this paper that the law of a single interface is not. More precisely, we consider the Ising model with mesh $δ$ in the Dobrushin square at $β=β_c-mδ$, where $m\ne0$ is fixed, and we prove that the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the law of the interface with respect to its critical law has moments of every positive and negative order, bounded uniformly in $δ$, so that the law of every subsequential scaling limit of the interface is mutually absolutely continuous with respect to that of $\mathrm{SLE}_3$. Our analysis explains the mechanism behind this result: the logarithmically growing specific heat (that is, the variance of the Hamiltonian, normalized by the number of edges) cancels between the full domain and the domain slit along the interface.

papers.title: Sustainability of TSFM Deployment and Pretraining: From Carbon Footprint Analysis to Mitigation via Pruning
papers.summary: Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) offer strong zero-shot forecasting capabilities, but their high pretraining cost raises a practical sustainability question: does this upfront investment pay off over a full deployment lifecycle, compared to supervised standalone models that must be periodically retrained? We model the cumulative carbon cost of different approaches across a realistic industrial scenario: Chronos-2 amortizes its pretraining cost within months for large or frequently queried deployments, but a classical model remains cheaper indefinitely for small or rarely queried ones. For cases where reducing the TSFM's own cost matters, we show that removing a single encoder block (7.9% of parameters) via a gradient-free pruning criterion yields a consistent 6 to 9% reduction in FLOPs, CO2 emissions, and latency, at essentially no cost to zero-shot forecasting performance across a 25-task benchmark.
papers.comment: 26 pages, 6 figures, accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop TS-LIMITS

papers.title: Hardy inequalities on the positive integer lattice: a dimensional transition
papers.summary: We determine exactly in which dimensions the sharp Hardy coefficient on the positive integer lattice agrees with that on the positive Euclidean cone, with Dirichlet conditions on every coordinate face. Equality holds in dimensions one and two, whereas the discrete coefficient is strictly smaller in every dimension at least three. An exact transformation identifies the lattice problem with a weighted Dirichlet problem on a cube. A tangential integration identity evaluates the defect of an explicit critical profile and proves the dimensional transition. The continuous coefficient remains the lower edge of the essential spectrum of the transformed operator; below that edge, the sharp discrete coefficient is a simple eigenvalue with a positive eigenfunction. In dimension three, an explicit supersolution places the coefficient strictly between twelve and forty-nine quarters. A representation on a product of three-dimensional spheres relates the spectral threshold to the local geometry of the transformed problem.

papers.title: Self-similar solutions for the gSQG patch equations
papers.summary: The inviscid generalized surface quasi-geostrophic (gSQG) equations are a family of active scalar equations parametrized by a scalar $α$ that includes the two-dimensional Euler equations ($α= 0)$ and the SQG equation $(α= 1)$. We prove that, for every $α\in (\frac{7}{4}, 2)$ and every $T > 0$, there exists a self-similar patch solution whose boundary is a smooth, unbounded graph for $0 \leq t < T$ and develops a corner singularity at time $T$.

papers.title: Non-singlets and the phase diagram of Matrix Quantum Mechanics
papers.summary: The quantum mechanics of one $N\times N$ Hermitian matrix in the infinite $N$ limit is well known to define a two-dimensional string theory when the quartic coupling constant $g$ is tuned to a special negative value $g_*$. We study the thermodynamics of this Matrix Quantum Mechanics (MQM), treating the SU$(N)$ symmetry as a global symmetry. Crucially, the non-singlets, i.e. states in non-trivial representations of SU$(N)$, implement the effects of vortices on the discretized worldsheets. This random lattice model has the low-temperature $c=1$ and high-temperature $c=0$ phases, with the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition separating them. We map out the phase diagram in the coupling--temperature plane, which is separated by the critical stability curve $T_c(g)$ extending from $g_*< g <0$. We study this curve using the non-perturbative matrix bootstrap and low- and high-temperature perturbation theory, which explain the thermal instability. At low temperatures, thermally excited non-singlets backreact on the Fermi sea of matrix eigenvalues, causing it to spill over. At high temperatures, the theory is described by an effective matrix integral obtained by dimensional reduction on the thermal circle; the eigenvalue distribution of the zero mode becomes unstable at the critical coupling. We conjecture that the BKT transition occurs at a special point on the critical curve and estimate its position. Finally, we switch to the regular square lattice and study the MQM-inspired Villain model, where the link factor is the one-dimensional propagator on a circle. Using Monte Carlo simulations, we map out the BKT transition in this model.

papers.title: Regularised RL improves sim-to-real transfer
papers.summary: Regularised reinforcement learning (RL) has provable robustness guarantees that should ease the transfer of policies from simulation to robots, known as sim-to-real. Yet, weakly regularised algorithms like Proximal Policy Optimisation (PPO) remain the de facto choice in sim-to-real pipelines, while the practical benefits of regularisation for transfer remain poorly characterised. In this work, we study the sim-to-real performance of commonly used RL algorithms, with the aim of characterising the effects of regularisation on robotic performance. To that end, we derive Soft MellowMax Actor-Critic (SMM-AC), a novel regularised RL algorithm based on the soft mellowmax value function, which carries strong robustness guarantees. On MuJoCo continuous control benchmarks, SMM-AC is competitive with baselines like Soft Actor-Critic (SAC). On real robots, SMM-AC achieves higher return, while exhibiting greater robustness to perturbations in observations, the environment, and dynamics than baselines. Together, these results demonstrate that regularised RL improves real-world policy deployment through better robustness to the sim-to-real gap, and changing real-world conditions.
papers.comment: 9 pages of main-body content, with supporting details in the appendices. Under submission

papers.title: Singular Geometry of Low-Rank Adaptation
papers.summary: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is now a standard approach to parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large neural networks. Its low-rank factorization is inherently non-identifiable, making LoRA a singular statistical model whose learning complexity cannot be described by parameter dimension alone. We study this complexity using the real log canonical threshold (RLCT) from singular learning theory and how it depends on both the low-rank parameterization and the pretrained network. Under a local linearization, LoRA induces a low-rank trace regression model whose Kullback--Leibler geometry is controlled by a forward-backward covariance, constructed from activations and backpropagated sensitivities at the adapted layer. This covariance determines which low-rank perturbations are statistically observable. When it is nondegenerate along the relevant low-rank directions, we recover the classical learning complexity of reduced-rank regression; when its kernel meets these directions, additional statistically indistinguishable parameters change the singular geometry. We characterize this geometry locally through observable tangent directions and a residual singularity, and globally through affine linear sections of determinantal varieties. The global learning complexity need not be determined at a ground-truth parameter, as singularities on another rank stratum can dominate. We also introduce a curvature-corrected multi-temperature estimator of the RLCT. Experiments on multilayer perceptron and transformer architectures reveal strongly layer-dependent forward-backward geometry and show that ambient covariance degeneracy does not imply degeneracy along the low-rank directions relevant to adaptation.

papers.title: Near-Optimal List Replicability from Littlestone Dimension
papers.summary: We study the list replicability number in the realizable PAC learning framework and prove that every concept class $H$ over a countable domain with Littlestone dimension $d$ and dual VC dimension $v^*$ satisfies \[ \mathrm{LR}(H)\leq 2^{O(d\min\{\log d,v^*\})}. \] This matches the worst-case lower bound of $2^{Ω(d)}$ up to a logarithmic factor in the exponent and exponentially improves the previous best upper bound $\mathrm{LR}(H)\le 2^{2^{O(d)}}$ of Bun, Livni, and Moran [FOCS 2020]. Unlike earlier bounds of $2^{O_ε(d^2)}$ for fixed accuracy $ε>0$ implied by the work of Ghazi, Golowich, Kumar, and Manurangsi [STOC 2021] and Lyu [STOC 2026], our bound is independent of $ε$. The $2^{O(d\log d)}$ bound follows from a new inductive framework for bounding list replicability that builds on the recent notion of irreducibility from differentially private learning. The $2^{O(dv^*)}$ bound follows from a simple globally stable learner that takes the majority vote of multiple empirical risk minimizers, with stability established using tools from stable regularity.

papers.title: Radiation damage and recovery of SiPMs exposed to low-momentum muon beams for innovative scintillation-based muon beam monitors
papers.summary: Silicon PhotoMultipliers (SiPMs) are among the standard devices for light detection in scintillator detectors. Some detector designs require these devices to be placed in radioactive areas or directly exposed to particle beams. Specifically, the damage from exposure to low-momentum muons is particularly important, as they have a high energy deposit and they have several applications in material science and particle physics. Eight SiPM models from different manufacturers were exposed to 29 MeV/c positive muons, with an intensity of O(10^6) muons/s for 13 hours, maximising the charge deposited in the depletion region. I-V curves were measured before/after irradiation and annealing; DCR and crosstalk analyses are ongoing, to extract dark count rate and optical crosstalk. Despite showing a measurable increase in dark current, the devices preserved operational stability. Thermal annealing has also been tested by heating the devices at 125°C, showing a recovery of the optimal SiPM features. This work is part of a collaboration between the University of Pavia and ISIS, to develop detectors for low-momentum muons (< 40 MeV/c), based on thin scintillators.
papers.comment: 5 pages, 8 figures, to be submitted to NIM-A (NDIP26 conference proceedings)

papers.title: Reimagining Enterprise RAG for Multi-Agent Systems: A Knowledge Layer That Organizes Before It Retrieves
papers.summary: Enterprises are deploying agentic AI across the software development lifecycle, and they need the behavioral logic of the systems they act on, not stakeholder documentation. A seven-agent reverse-engineering pipeline recovered this logic, processing 241 repositories across 18 services into thousands of artifacts describing scope, journeys, rules and acceptance criteria. Recovery does not confer usability. Entities like offer, eligibility, and activation recur across services under a shared vocabulary, related in name but operationally distinct, so one end-to-end journey implicates over a thousand near-identical rules that must not be conflated. Flat vector retrieval fails, returning an identical rule from the wrong service at high similarity with no signal of error. Content-level ontology, the traditional remedy, did not exist, and relating every occurrence of recurring entities would have cost more than the engagement and not survived a release cycle. We place the ontology at the artifact level. In this machine-generated corpus, each artifact retains its producer, component, service, domain and type, provenance that disambiguates before content is read. We present a knowledge layer that organizes before retrieving: a self-describing catalog, a sparse metadata registry, and a navigation hypergraph defined over artifacts rather than extracted entities. Queries resolve to artifact identifiers that constrain vector search, so the competing rule from another service is absent rather than outranked, making disambiguation structural, not statistical. Built in under a week and admitting new services by convention, the layer serves SDLC agents, developers, quality engineers and analysts. It supported root-cause analysis and resolution of 100+ production defects with developer verification and attributed 35 release regression failures to specific rules and services.

papers.title: Mixed Engression: Distributional Regression for Multivariate Mixed-Type Responses
papers.summary: Estimating the conditional distribution of multivariate responses with continuous and binary components requires capturing their dependence, respecting their different supports, and accommodating potentially heavy-tailed continuous outcomes. We propose mixed engression, which fits a continuous generator using energy losses induced by bounded discrepancies and then thresholds its soft binary outputs to produce mixed-response samples. Because the discrepancies are bounded, the population objective remains well defined without response-moment assumptions. However, we show that the full-response energy distance for the complete response vector can tend to zero before thresholding yet remain bounded away from zero afterward as response dimensions grow. A separate energy loss on the entire binary vector captures discrepancies obscured by the full-response comparison and controls the effect of thresholding. The generator is therefore fitted using an augmented energy loss that combines the full-response and binary components. Under compositional smoothness of the structural functions and a uniform threshold-margin condition, we derive nonasymptotic bounds on the final sampler's full-response error for sparse ReLU estimators of models driven by Gaussian or Student-t structural noise, yielding polynomial convergence rates up to logarithmic factors. We also establish consistency when the covariate, response, and noise dimensions grow under suitable conditions. Simulations show improved accuracy relative to the comparison methods under the full-response energy distance, including in heavy-tailed settings. Moderate binary augmentation substantially improves binary-distribution accuracy while largely preserving full-response accuracy.

papers.title: Neural LoFi with Backward Coupling: A Spectral Theory of Cross-Layer Feature Learning
papers.summary: During joint training, backpropagation allows later layers to reshape earlier representations, a feedback mechanism absent from purely layer-wise learning. We extend Neural Low-Degree Filtering (Neural LoFi), a recently proposed layer-wise spectral surrogate for feature learning, to capture this interaction. Starting from the exact backpropagation gradients, we derive a local coupling between a neuron's incoming weights and its corresponding next-layer column. In a controlled small-initialization regime with smooth activations and fixed surroundings, these dynamics amplify singular modes of a cross-layer correlation operator. Each growing mode pairs an earlier feature with an upper-layer response through shared neuron coefficients. This motivates a backward-coupling algorithm in which upper-layer sensitivities generate sample-dependent effective labels for earlier spectral steps, while corrected features refine upward transmission. A function-space variational principle characterizes the selected feature-response pairs by maximizing the label correlation of their product under kernel-norm constraints. For three-layer networks, we derive self-consistent continuous-time dynamics for the filtered hidden-layer features, the activation kernels, and the network output under the proposed backward coupling. In a hierarchical multi-index model, we establish a feature-recovery separation: backward coupling recovers lower-layer directions invisible to the original forward label-weighted statistic. The linear specialization recovers residual-dependent singular-mode dynamics, while paired modes provide a dynamical mechanism for linked low-rank covariance components consistent with the rainbow-network picture. Experiments with fully connected and convolutional networks on binary CIFAR-10 show improved accuracy over forward Neural LoFi at matched widths.

papers.title: OpenStripe supports open-set identification and spatial stripe profiling in wild Amur tigers
papers.summary: Non-invasive camera-trap monitoring of endangered wildlife requires open-set individual identification---grouping field images into identities without predefined classes or a known population size---yet pose deformation and cluttered backgrounds complicate image comparison. Here, we present OpenStripe, a multi-agent framework that reconstructs canonical two-dimensional (2D) tiger torso patterns and encodes four interpretable local stripe structures: breakpoints, bifurcations, irregular structures, and round structures. We evaluated OpenStripe on 100 camera-trap records from 28 wild Amur tigers (Panthera tigris altaica), representing nearly one-third of the documented population in the Northeast China Tiger and Leopard National Park. Combining all four complementary structures enabled automatic identity grouping with 0.90 matched accuracy and a 0.85 adjusted Rand index (ARI), outperforming 49 baseline configurations under the same backend (up to 0.43 accuracy and 0.14 ARI). In addition, results from OpenStripe indicate that stripe similarity in Amur tigers declines with geographic distance and suggest that traits such as fractal dimension and inter-stripe spacing are associated with geographic proximity. OpenStripe thus provides an interpretable representation that connects automated individual grouping with spatial phenotypic profiling in wild populations.
papers.comment: 14 pages, 4 figures. Code and nonspatial data: https://github.com/Yichun-Peng/OpenStripe

papers.title: Magnons and excitons from Bethe-Salpeter equation and its application to graphene-based magnets
papers.summary: With the recent isolation of two-dimensional semiconducting magnetic materials, the theoretical study of spin-flip collective excitations (magnons) along with spin-conserving electron-hole bound pairs (excitons) has become particularly relevant. Describing both types of quasiparticles within the same theoretical framework is possible, in principle, but the well-established many-body formalism for the calculation of excitons, based on the intertwined Bethe-Salpeter and Hedin's equations, is not satisfactory for magnons, since the usual approximations produce a spurious gapped Goldstone mode. Here, we show that excitons and magnons can be computed on the same footing under the same Bethe-Salpeter formalism, while respecting the gapless Goldstone mode for magnons. We demonstrate how this can be achieved through the evaluation of the full Bethe-Salpeter equation, beyond the Tamm-Dancoff approximation in model Hamiltonians. As an example, we apply it to ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic graphene, faithfully represented by the extended Hubbard model. Our results clarify the roles of on-site and non-local interactions in exciton and magnon appearance and identify consistency requirements relevant to extending the approach to first-principles calculations.

papers.title: Local Polynomial Estimation in Irregular Correlated Random Coefficient Panel Data Models
papers.summary: We study estimation of the average partial effect (APE) in an irregular correlated random coefficients panel data model in which the time dimension equals the number of random coefficients, $T=p$, and the density function is degenerate. We extend Graham and Powell (2012) in two directions. First, we allow the density of $d_i=\det(X_i)$ to vanish or diverge at the origin at the polynomial rate $|d|^{a}$ with $a>-1$, and show that the aggregate time effects and the APE remain identified for every such $a$, extending earlier work studying the case $a = 0$. Second, we propose a three-step estimator: an $m$th-order local polynomial regression over the stayers for the time effects; a local polynomial fit of the conditional mean coefficient just outside the trimming threshold; and an imputation step that extrapolates the latter into the stayer region rather than discarding stayers. We establish joint asymptotic normality in three regimes determined by the sign of $a$, and obtain a convergence rate approaching $n^{-(m+1)/(2m+3)}$ when $a=0$, against $n^{-1/3}$ for Graham and Powell (2012), whose estimator is the special case $m=0$, $a=0$. The results show that smoothness of the underlying conditional expectations can be traded for a faster convergence rate in irregularly identified models. Simulations confirm lower bias and root mean squared error across designs. We redo the overidentification analysis of a markup model in Raval (2023), allowing for correlated random elasticities.

papers.title: The Galactic Center Gamma-Ray Excess and the Look-Elsewhere Effect
papers.summary: The origin of the excess of GeV gamma-rays in the Milky Way's galactic center observed by Fermi-LAT has been an open question for nearly two decades. The two leading interpretations of this signal are that it is produced either by annihilating dark matter (DM), or arises from unresolved point sources, such as a novel population of millisecond pulsars. In both scenarios, uncertainties and limitations in the modeling of galactic diffuse gamma-ray emission, such as the steady-state approximation of cosmic ray (CR) propagation and assumption of an axisymmetric distribution of CRs, complicate the interpretation of the galactic center excess (GCE). Simulations with full magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) and CR transport can provide a new avenue for understanding the astrophysical phenomena that drive galactic diffuse gamma-ray emission. We utilize MHD simulations of Milky Way analogs with time-dependent, spectrally-resolved CR transport to reconstruct diffuse gamma-ray emission. Comparing instantaneous emission to a time-averaged baseline, we find residuals up to several times larger than the Fermi GCE, with a wide range of spectral shapes and spatial morphologies. At some simulation snapshots, the spectrum and morphology of the residuals resemble the Fermi GCE. Our results suggest that the Fermi GCE may be a manifestation of the look-elsewhere effect- a transient fluctuation in diffuse emission from stellar sources, observed at an inopportune moment- and motivate the development of new Fermi-LAT analysis templates that account for time-dependent CR transport.

papers.title: Out-of-sample prediction in SEM: A simulation-based comparison of maximum likelihood and (consistent) partial least squares
papers.summary: Structural equation modeling (SEM) is widely used to study relationships among unobserved constructs. Over recent years, the interest in computing predictions with SEM has grown. Different prediction procedures have been proposed for this purpose, including MLpredict, which is based on maximum likelihood (ML) estimation, and PLS(c)predict, which is based on partial least squares (PLS). The out-of-sample predictive performances of these procedures have not yet been compared. In our work, we conduct a comprehensive Monte Carlo study to compare out-of-sample predictions of MLpredict and PLS(c)predict for indicators associated with endogenous constructs, so-called operative predictions. Here, we vary key design factors regarding, for instance, the strengths of structural relations, the training sample size, and the construct types in the data generating processes, which determine the presence or absence of construct misspecification. Across the investigated conditions, MLpredict and PLS(c)predict exhibit similar predictive performance according to two assessment criteria, indicating that neither procedure is uniformly superior for operative prediction. Out-of-sample predictive performance is driven mainly by the strength of the relations between the variables, whereas training sample size and construct misspecification have comparatively little influence on it. An exception is the occasionally inflated prediction error of PLScpredict, which is in line with previous findings for ordinal indicators. Overall, our results suggest that, in the studied setting, fine-grained methodological differences between traditional SEM and PLS-based procedures matter less for out-of-sample predictive performance than properties of the data generating process, such as the coefficient of determination of endogenous constructs.

papers.title: Communicating with the Entire Population: Machine Translation of Emergency Alerts and Warnings
papers.summary: It is essential that we communicate with the entirety of an affected population during a crisis, including those who do not speak a region's dominant language(s). Commercial Translation tools offer a tempting solution to broaden access and can provide a lifeline when no other resources are available. However, Emergency response managers often operate in the dark regarding the quality and adequacy of these automated outputs. In this paper, we conduct a nationwide survey of emergency managers to understand their current workflows, perspectives, and operational challenges. We then evaluate commercial translation tools against these needs, shedding light on their utility and offering practical guidance on how and when these tools can be safely used in emergency response.
papers.comment: In Proceedings of the Language Technologies for Crisis Preparedness and Response (LT4CPR Workshop), Hengqin, Zhuhai, China. Association for Computational Linguistics. Nov 2026

papers.title: Hardware-Friendly Estimation of LCU-Based Expectation Values via Quantum-to-Classical Workload Shifting
papers.summary: Estimating the expectation value of an observable $O$ for a quantum state evolved under a general, possibly non-unitary, operator $A$ is a fundamental task in quantum simulation, chemistry, and variational algorithms. Existing linear-combination-of-unitaries (LCU) approaches implement $A$ on hardware, requiring ancilla qubits, controlled unitaries and, in randomized variants, fresh circuit executions for every Monte Carlo sample. These costs are prohibitive on NISQ and early fault-tolerant devices. We propose HERMES (Hardware-Efficient Reusable Measurements for Estimating LCU-based expectation valueS), which moves the processing of $A$ entirely to the classical domain. Expanding $A$ and $O$ in the Pauli basis and sampling pairs of Pauli terms classically, HERMES rewrites $μ= \mathrm{Tr}(OAρA^{\dagger})/\mathrm{Tr}(AρA^{\dagger})$ as a ratio of weighted sums of Pauli expectation values on the unmodified state $ρ$, with no ancillas, controlled unitaries, or quantum implementation of $A$. A two-level measurement reduction scheme (Pauli deduplication and commuting-group partitioning) bounds the number of distinct measurement settings independently of the sample count, unlike randomized LCU methods whose circuit executions grow linearly with it. On ground-state energy estimation of $\mathrm{H}_2$ and $\mathrm{LiH}$ via imaginary-time evolution, HERMES matches or beats Pauli single-ancilla LCU baseline using shallow circuits with no two-qubit gates beyond state preparation under qubit-wise commuting grouping. It is also more robust to noise and completes a noisy $\mathrm{LiH}$ simulation infeasible for the baseline, at the cost of classical overhead growing with the number of Pauli terms in $A$.

papers.title: Physics Informed Neural Network for Multi-dimensional Turbulent Self-gravitating Flows
papers.summary: Molecular clouds exhibit complex, multi-scale dynamics driven by the interplay of turbulence, self-gravity, and gas pressure. Modelling these systems with conventional grid-based methods becomes increasingly expensive as spatial resolution and dimensionality increase. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) offer a mesh-free alternative by incorporating the governing equations directly into the training objective, but their ability to model realistic turbulent self-gravitating flows remains largely unexplored. We apply PINNs to isothermal molecular clouds initialized with astrophysically motivated turbulent velocity fields, considering subsonic and supersonic evolution in two and three dimensions. We benchmark the predicted density and velocity fields against the finite-volume code Athena++. PINNs accurately recover the global evolution of the flow over multiple free-fall times across turbulent realizations, Mach numbers, and dimensionalities. Their training cost also exhibits weak dependence on spatial resolution, increasing by less than 25% from 128^3 to 1024^3 in our experiments. These results demonstrate that PINNs can model substantially more realistic self-gravitating turbulent flows than previously explored and provide a promising complementary framework for studying these systems.

papers.title: Finite-Temperature Transconductance of Multiterminal Josephson Junctions with Topological Andreev Spectra
papers.summary: Multiterminal Josephson junctions (MTJJs) provide a controllable platform for engineering topological Andreev spectra. At zero temperature, Andreev bound states (ABSs) with nonzero Chern numbers give rise to quantized transconductance between superconducting terminals. We derive the finite-temperature transconductance of MTJJs using linear-response theory. We first demonstrate the destructive role of temperature: changes in the thermal occupations of the ABSs destroy exact transconductance quantization. We then show that finite temperature can also play a constructive role by making the transconductance sensitive to finite-energy topological crossings hidden from the zero-temperature response. Our results establish the thermal limitations of transconductance quantization and identify finite-temperature transport as a probe of otherwise inaccessible topology in Andreev spectra.

papers.title: Modular optical fault-tolerant quantum computation via an interface between verified resources and online logical operations
papers.summary: We introduce a factory--processor interface architecture for modular optical fault-tolerant quantum computation that separates code-dependent encoded-resource preparation from reusable online logical processing on a common Gaussian optical processor. Beyond encoded resources, the interface specifies logical outputs, code-to-mode mapping, measurement roles, frame updates, verification records, and resource-injection boundaries. As a concrete realization, we combine an offline verified Bell-resource factory based on a recursively concatenated $C_4$ code with physical Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill (GKP) qubits with an online time-domain measurement-based quantum computation (MBQC) processor. Under the specified additive-displacement-noise model and fixed postselection policy, simulations support the finite-level logical Bell-error ordering $P_5<P_4<P_3<P_2$ at 12.25 dB of effective GKP displacement-noise quality, both with and without the prescribed additional post-injection displacement noise. At 15.6 dB and $L=2$, a separate fixed-sample evaluation gives one-sided 95$\%$ Clopper--Pearson upper bounds below $10^{-5}$ for both conditions under the binomial model. The interface supports address-tracked injection, transversal CNOT and logical Bell-measurement constructions, and logical SWAP and Hadamard constructions with tracked code permutations. Given advance resource preparation and sufficient routing parallelism, increasing the concatenation level expands parallel encoded-resource width without increasing the protected online sequence length of these constructions. These results identify a modular route to lower logical error rates while retaining a common Gaussian MBQC operation set with shallow online processing.

papers.title: Modelling kNN-CDFs of biased tracers in redshift space using hybrid Lagrangian bias expansion
papers.summary: Higher-order statistics are becoming increasingly useful in clustering studies of the large-scale structure (LSS) of the universe. The kNN-CDFs are one such higher-order statistic, sensitive to all N-point correlations and easy to compute on data. Utilising their statistical gains for cosmological inference requires modelling them accurately for the tracer of interest. We use the hybrid Lagrangian bias expansion to enable this modelling in redshift space, building and validating the pipeline on Quijote simulations. We show that the kNN-CDFs of a luminous red galaxy (LRG)-like sample can be modelled down to scales as small as r = 10 Mpc/h, with the minimum reliable scale increasing with nearest-neighbour order. Moreover, the model parameters inferred from the kNN-CDFs also describe the galaxy power spectrum P(k), indicating model consistency across the two statistics and the feasibility of combining them. Fisher forecasts for galaxy auto clustering show that combining P(k) and kNN-CDFs improves constraints on all parameters relative to either statistic alone. Relative to P(k), the constraints on $b_3$ improve the most, while those on $σ_8$ and $Ω_m$ improve by factors of 3.5 and 1.7, respectively. Including galaxy-matter cross clustering alongside galaxy auto clustering further improves the Fisher constraints from both P(k) and kNN-CDFs, with their combination yielding the tightest constraints overall. Relative to P(k), the largest improvement from this combination is found for $b_2$, while the constraints on $σ_8$ and $Ω_m$ improve by factors of 4.2 and 1.7, respectively. These results demonstrate the applicability of the hybrid Lagrangian bias framework to model the kNN-CDFs of biased tracers in redshift space, and the potential of combining higher-order and two-point statistics to extract cosmological information.

papers.title: SPOOK: Sparse Pixel Optimization for Off-Manifold Knowledge in Vision Encoders
papers.summary: Modern vision encoders are widely used as semantic representations, but the relationship between embedding similarity and human-visible semantics can become unclear far from the natural-image manifold. We probe this regime in a black-box setting by applying sparse pixel edits to blank canvases with a simple pixel-level hill-climbing procedure. Across ImageNet and Flickr30k, we evaluate whether these edited blank canvases can retrieve chosen targets in multimodal contrastive encoders and self-supervised visual encoders. On OpenCLIP, inputs optimized toward class prompts achieve strong top-1 and top-5 targeted retrieval performance; on DINOv3, inputs optimized toward class prototypes achieve high target alignment and near-top prototype ranks. These results show that sparse edits on otherwise blank, visually non-semantic inputs can enter target semantic basins in both language-aligned and self-supervised visual representation spaces. Our findings identify a shared off-manifold failure mode of modern vision encoders and suggest sparse blank-canvas optimization as a simple probe of representation geometry.
papers.comment: 12 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables, and 14 pages of Supplementary Material with 8 figures

papers.title: The Physics of the Cold and Warm Interstellar Medium Through Radio Recombination Lines
papers.summary: The interplay between star formation and the interstellar medium (ISM) gives rise to a feedback cycle that is one of the key drivers of galaxy evolution. The coldest gas in the ISM provides the fuel for star formation, and, in turn, the ISM is affected by feedback in the form of photons, shocks, and cosmic rays. Radio recombination lines (RRLs) offer a unique way of characterizing the gas in the ISM as extinction free probes of the gas kinematics, density, temperature, and radiation field. Hydrogen RRLs (HRRLs) probe gas where hydrogen is ionized, while carbon RRLs (CRRLs) probe cold gas in the HI-to-H$_{2}$ transition layers. The superb sensitivity, spatial resolution, large field of view, and frequency resolution and coverage of the Square Kilometre Array (SKA) will allow for efficient observations of RRLs, that will make significant impacts to the study of the diffuse ISM. By observing RRLs with the SKA we will be able to determine the thermal and turbulent balance, chemical enrichment, sizes, and ionization rate of the cold and ionized gases from degree-scales down to arcsecond scales in our Galaxy.
papers.comment: Published in Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII), 2026 (arXiv:2606.20366). Report-no:AASKAII/Salas01

papers.title: Diversity of planetary origins and compositions traced by stellar abundance differences of co-natal star systems
papers.summary: Co-natal stars, wide binaries that form from the same molecular cloud, should harbor the same stellar composition. Observations indicate stellar abundance differences in a small fraction of these co-natal systems. The stellar abundance differences have been attributed to the ingestion of planets by their host stars. We analyze a previous sample of co-natal stars to determine the composition of the planets that were ingested. The abundance differences in these co-natal pairs can show a positive abundance difference of the refractory elements (Fe, Mg, Si) paired with a positive, zero, or negative abundance difference of volatiles (O, C, S). Positive trends of refractory and volatile abundance differences can be explained (at minimum) with the ingestion of a single planet by one of the stars. Positive trends of refractory abundance differences paired with zero or negative abundance differences of oxygen and carbon imply that both stars are required to ingest planets formed at different locations (interior/exterior to the water and/or C-grain evaporation front). Some systems show a sulfur abundance difference that is a factor of a few lower than the abundance difference of Fe, Si, and Mg, even though sulfur is accreted via the moderately volatile compound FeS. This can be explained by the migration of one of the planets across the FeS evaporation front, where the planet first accretes large amounts of sulfur and then no sulfur, while still accreting the other refractory elements before being ingested by its host star. Our study shows that the planetary compositions derived from the detailed stellar abundances can explain the measured abundance differences of co-natal stars, giving a handle on the composition of exoplanets. At the same time it implies very different planetary compositions caused by the different formation location of these planets, in agreement with planet formation models.
papers.comment: Accepted by A&A, 11 pages, 3 figures, 3 pages appendix

papers.title: Kazhdan--Lusztig Polynomials for permutations with $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(1)=3$ and Irreducible Singular Locus
papers.summary: We determine the Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)$ for permutations $w$ such that $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(1)=3$ and the Schubert variety $X_w$ has irreducible singular locus. Let $h=h(w)$ be the minimum height $w(a)-w(d)$ of a $3412$-occurrence in $w$ at positions $a<b<c<d$, with $h=1$ when no such occurrence exists. We show that $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)=1+q^h+q^{h+1}$ if exactly one of the patterns $3412$ and $4231$ occurs, and $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)=1+q+q^h$ if both patterns occur. In the latter case, $h>1$. This proves the irreducible singular locus case of a 2009 conjecture of Billey and Weed.

papers.title: $G_0$ of complete split toric varieties
papers.summary: We compute the Grothendieck group of coherent sheaves for complete split toric surfaces having a smooth 2-dimensional cone in its fan. We show that it is free abelian, of rank equal to the number of rays in the fan. We give a partial generalization of this to all complete split toric varieties.

papers.title: The Two-Dimensional Narrow Escape Problem with Deterministic Initial Condition: Mean Escape Time and Escape location probabilities
papers.summary: This paper presents a rigorous asymptotic analysis of the two-dimensional narrow escape problem for a Brownian particle initiated at a deterministic position x. While we address the mean escape time, the main novelty lies in our derivation of the asymptotic escape distribution. We derive explicit asymptotic formulas that characterize the dependence of the escape behavior on the relative configuration of the starting point and the window centers. These results remain valid as the starting position approaches the boundary windows and include refined error estimates. The formulas are obtained with two independent methods, each of them having their own interest. A central feature of this work is the rigorous treatment of the underlying mixed boundary value problems in the absence of a contact angle at the escape window boundaries. By leveraging recent results on the maximal regularity of the gradient of the solutions of such mixed boundary value problems, we ensure the analytical validity of our approach despite the inherent loss of regularity of these solutions at the escape window boundaries. Finally, we apply these general results to provide a full sharp asymptotic equivalents for regimes where window sizes scale at specific relative rates.

papers.title: Multi-Timescale Context-Aware Radio Resource Optimization for Harmonious NTN-TN Coexistence: A Digital Twin and Open RAN Enabled Framework
papers.summary: Coexistence between non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) and terrestrial networks (TNs) is essential for future wireless systems, but terrestrial downlink transmissions can generate harmful aggregate interference at low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite receivers. We present DT-STABLE, an Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN)-enabled, digital twin (DT)-assisted framework for context-aware NTN-TN coexistence. Using site-specific information, the DT estimates interference at LEO satellites, enabling proactive management with reduced real-time measurement overhead. We formulate joint beam activation and user association under RF-chain limits, load balancing, and aggregate satellite interference constraints; prove NP-hardness; and develop an efficient DT-guided scheduling algorithm. DT-STABLE couples short-timescale radio resource adaptation with periodic mid- and long-timescale DT updates through standardized O-RAN interfaces. Site-specific 28 GHz simulations under worst-case satellite geometry and low elevation angles show that DT-STABLE balances rate and interference utility, achieving 89.63% interference-to-noise ratio (INR) satisfaction and a mean sum rate of 210.96 bps/Hz, with nearly 100% INR satisfaction when satellite protection is prioritized. The framework reduces beam measurement overhead by 99.71% relative to exhaustive sweeping and achieves up to 33.1 times lower runtime than the Gurobi-based exact optimization benchmark.
papers.comment: Submitted to IEEE for possible publication

papers.title: Research of signs of star formation in three S0 galaxies - members of isolated pairs
papers.summary: We obtained and analyzed long-slit spectra of three lenticular galaxies with optical rings: PGC 48114, ESO 234-011, and ESO 444-076. Ionized gas was detected in all of them. In PGC 48114, the excitation mechanism of the ionized gas differs along the ring, despite the consistent kinematics of the ionized gas and stars, as we showed earlier. Narrow-band images of PGC 48114 in the H$α$ and [NII]$λ$6583 emission lines revealed a star formation arc in the northwestern part of the ring. In ESO 234-011 and ESO 444-076, the ionized gas along the long slit is shock-excited and have kinematic discrepancy with the stars. This implies accretion of matter at an angle to the main disk of the S0 galaxies, which likely inhibits ongoing star formation. The companions of these S0 galaxies are late-type galaxies with extensive ongoing star formation. These companions may be the sources of the gas, or each pair may be feeding from a common gas reservoir.
papers.comment: 23 pages, 15 figures, 8 tables. Accepted in Res. Astron. Astrophys

papers.title: Traces of Green's functions on $\mathbb{H}^q$ over point-hypersurface pairs
papers.summary: The famous algebraicity conjecture of Gross and Zagier for the values at CM points of higher Green's functions was recently proven by Bruinier, Li and Yang. Motivated by this the values of the automorphic Green's function at pairs of special points in hyperbolic $3$-space $\mathbb{H}^3$ were studied by Herrero, Imamoglu, von Pippich and Schwagenscheidt, and an analogous algebraicity result for traces of Green's functions was established. In this paper, we consider higher automorphic Green's functions $G_{s}(P,Q)$ on hyperbolic $q$-space $\mathbb{H}^q$ for $q\geq 2$ when the spectral parameter $s$ is a positive even integer, and prove an explicit finite formula for their traces over geodesic hypersurfaces in one of the variables. This formula provides a geometric interpretation of the traces of Green's functions for every choice of a point in $\mathbb{H}^q$ for the second variable. As an application, we obtain rationality results when the second variable is evaluated at a special point providing further evidence that such results for traces of Green's functions do not depend on any underlying complex structure.

papers.title: A Short Proof of Zhang's Conjecture on Stack-Sortable Permutations
papers.summary: We give a short proof of Zhang's conjecture that the number of stack-sortable permutations of length $n + 1$ which end in their smallest element is equal to the $n$-th Motzkin number.

papers.title: Minimal unitary representations of time-invariant causal quantum channels
papers.summary: In this work, we study quantum channels that respect causality in single-input-single-output linear time-invariant systems. We show that positive semidefinite kernels satisfying certain analyticity constraints, which we call Schur-class kernels, provide a suitable description of such channels through multiplicative maps (Schur multipliers). Using the Moore-Aronszajn Theorem, we establish that these multipliers admit a minimal analytic Stinespring representation, which, in the unital case, is given by multiplication by a left inner function. We then relate the output rank of pure-state inputs to the dimension of the associated reproducing kernel Hilbert space. Using de Branges-Rovnyak realizations, we derive a stability criterion for the existence of two-sided inner completions of these vector-valued functions. We further show that the adjoint of the Julia embedding associated with the realization is minimal, and that its characteristic function essentially coincides with the canonical two-sided inner completion suggested by the Beurling-Lax-Halmos Theorem. Finally, we provide algorithms for explicitly computing minimal two-sided inner completions in the case of finite McMillan degree.

papers.title: On the Limits of Sparse Linear Model with Shuffled Differential Privacy
papers.summary: Sparse linear regression is a fundamental problem in high-dimensional statistics, and its private counterparts leave a large gap between the central and the local model of differential privacy. Shuffled differential privacy (SDP) sits between the two, offering accuracy closer to the central model without the trust requirement of a central curator. This paper studies sparse linear regression under both non-interactive and interactive SDP protocols. In the non-interactive setting, any non-interactive $(ε,δ)$-SDP protocol is shown to incur an $\ell_2$-norm estimation error of $Ω( \frac{\sqrt{dk}}{nε} )$ with dimension $d$, sparsity $k$, and $n$ users, revealing an inherent dimensionality barrier. In addition, a non-interactive algorithm is proposed that achieves an $\ell_2$-norm upper bound of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}( \sqrt{\frac{k}{n}} + \frac{d\sqrt{k}}{nε})$. To overcome this barrier, we turn to the interactive user-level setting, where each user holds $m$ samples. A two-round interactive algorithm is developed that first recovers the support through a heavy hitter step and then estimates the parameter, achieving an error of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}( \sqrt{\frac{k}{nm}} + \frac{k}{n\sqrt{m}ε} )$ with no polynomial dependence on $d$. Furthermore, by extending the score attack framework to user-level data, a new lower bound $Ω( \sqrt{\frac{k\log(d/k)}{nm}} + \frac{k\log(d/k)}{n\sqrt{m}ε} )$ is established for any user-level $(ε,δ)$-DP, showing that the proposed algorithm is near-optimal with only a gap of the factor $\log(d/k)$.

papers.title: The boosted loop-erased random walk
papers.summary: We consider a near-critical version of loop-erased random walk (LERW) by boosting the weight of the underlying random walk according to its length before loop-erasure. We construct the scaling limit in natural parametrization in the two-dimensional unit disk and the three-dimensional unit ball. The boosted scaling limit undergoes a phase transition in mutual absolute continuity with the classical LERW scaling limit; in the disk the transition occurs at boost rate $m^2=π^2/4$. As the boost increases, the curve becomes macroscopically space-filling, in the sense that unvisited cubes have side length $O(m^{-1})$, while its Hausdorff dimension at each finite boost is unchanged. These results are motivated by Makarov--Smirnov's questions on near-critical lattice models. In the planar chordal setting, we also construct a continuum loop tilt below the spectral threshold of the domain and calculate its Loewner driving function.

papers.title: Pesin's entropy formula on attractors with continuous invariant splittings
papers.summary: Under quantitative asymptotic hyperbolicity assumptions, we prove the existence of hyperbolic ergodic invariant probability measures satisfying Pesin's entropy formula for $C^1$ diffeomorphisms whose attractors admit extendable continuous invariant splittings. No dominated splitting is required on the attractor. For $C^{1+α}$ diffeomorphisms, the resulting measures are SRB measures. Our results apply to mostly expanding partially hyperbolic systems and to systems with strictly separated Lyapunov exponents under suitable statistical assumptions. We also construct examples with hyperbolic SRB measures of full support on attractors admitting no nontrivial dominated splitting, demonstrating the applicability of our criteria beyond results that require domination.

papers.title: KrishokTech: A Bengali Agricultural Advisory System with Explicit Authorization Controls
papers.summary: For agricultural advisory, generating an answer is only part of the problem: the system must also control unsafe requests, work with limited connectivity, and accommodate changing guidance. KRISHOKTECH is a Bengali agricultural advisory system built around an explicit authorization boundary around generation. Before retrieval, normalization and rule-based admission checks refer policy-covered high-risk requests and ask for a crop when treatment intent is underspecified. The system then binds retrieval to a single crop and asks for confirmation when the text and image indicate different crops. After generation, a narrow verifier removes dosage claims not supported by retrieved BARI/BRRI evidence. Agricultural guidance is kept in an external evidence index that can be updated without retraining the generator, while browser-side vision and local retrieval reduce connectivity requirements. The interface makes these decisions visible as ASK, CONFIRM, REFER, and DROP, together with their evidence. On 200 farmer queries and 400 stress queries, the controls halted underspecified requests and reduced cross-crop retrieval violations from 36.5% to 0% under the tested alias filter. Mismatch detection caught 453 of 454 text-image conflicts, while the verifier caught 114 of 118 inserted dosage errors. The demonstration shows how these controls govern the path from request to delivered advice.

papers.title: Sounding Surgical Instrument Localisation through Audio-Visual Correspondence
papers.summary: Surgical scene understanding is a prerequisite for context-aware and intelligent systems in the operating room. Current methods rely mostly on visual data, while acoustic sensing has shown potential to provide complementary information on surgical activity. First approaches for the localisation of surgical activity relied on microphone arrays and acoustic beamforming. This work investigates whether the active instrument can be localized from a single microphone and a camera by learning the correspondence between the appearance and the sound of surgical instruments, without annotating its position. We adapt weakly supervised audio-visual localisation, which learns from the co-occurrence of image and sound, to the surgical setting. We record simulated surgical actions, sawing, drilling, and chiseling, and train the model on these recordings without any spatial annotation to produce a heatmap over the sounding tool. We extend the training objective by two terms: a silence term, which suppresses the output for silence and background noise, and a composite term, which trains the model to select the sounding one of two visible instruments. The model localizes the active instrument on an independent corpus recorded with a different camera and microphone, in which instrument positions were obtained by optical tracking. It separates tool activity from silence and background noise and can attribute sound correctly when two tools are present. Audio-visual correspondence learned from in-domain recordings connects the sound of a surgical action to the instrument that produces it, using a single microphone and a camera. This proof of concept introduces a novel paradigm that enables the detection and localisation of surgical activity without manual annotations.

papers.title: The GAPS Programme at TNG LXXXI. The puzzle of the HeI absorption signal in the atmosphere of V1298 Tau b with GIARPS@TNG
papers.summary: Atmospheric escape shapes close-in planets mostly in their first tens of Myr. The young V1298Tau system (10-30Myr) is a benchmark for investigating photoevaporation and planetary evolution at early stages. The metastable HeI near-infrared triplet is a key proxy for atmospheric escape. We aim to detect and characterise HeI in the extended atmosphere of V1298Taub. We analysed four transits over a 4-year baseline using GIARPS (GIANO-B + HARPS-N) at the Telescopio Nazionale Galileo. We re-derived the projected spin-orbit angle by modelling the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect. Using simultaneous optical and near-infrared high-resolution transmission spectroscopy of V1298Taub, we monitored the HeI triplet alongside key chromospheric indicators ($\log R'_{HK}$, H$α$, and NaI) to disentangle stellar activity from planetary evaporation. While the stellar spectra show significant night-to-night variability, transmission spectroscopy reveals persistent HeI absorption across all four epochs. This contrasts with H$α$ and NaI, observed over two nights with simultaneous HARPS-N monitoring, which fluctuate between emission and absorption due to stellar activity. The consistent presence of HeI over 4 years may suggest a planetary origin, despite stellar-driven depth modulation. ATES hydrodynamic simulations show that stellar XUV flux variations modulate the HeI absorption depth and equivalent width. Furthermore, stellar wind fluctuations likely drive the observed night-to-night variability of the exospheric structure. The detection of HeI across all epochs may support planetary evaporation, despite modulation by stellar activity. Our results underscore that disentangling a planetary signal from stellar contamination remains challenging for highly active hosts; securing the planetary nature of the HeI signature requires activity monitoring and full transit coverage to establish a robust baseline.
papers.comment: 20 pages, accepted for publication in A&A

papers.title: Large deviations and applications in homogeneous dynamics
papers.summary: We consider the left translation action of an element $a$ on a finite-volume semisimple homogeneous space $G/Γ$, where $\operatorname{Ad}(a)$ is diagonalizable over $\mathbb{R}$. Assuming exponential mixing, we prove a sub-Gaussian large-deviation estimate for compactly supported smooth test functions. As an application, we prove effective uniqueness of the measure of maximal entropy. We also obtain quantitative pointwise equidistribution for Haar-almost every point on each full expanding horosphere.

papers.title: HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency
papers.summary: Agent harnesses repeatedly invoke reasoning after tool feedback, even when an earlier call has already fixed the next action. We introduce HarnessMM (Harness Minus Minus), a method for improving harness token efficiency through guarded decision reuse and recursive self-improvement (RSI). RSI iteratively refines companion harness configurations from training feedback, with validation selecting the configuration for deployment. A controller at the model-tool boundary reuses resolved decisions to replace later reasoning callbacks while actor weights remain fixed. Executable Decision Graphs store exact actions, literal arguments, causal dependencies, and public guards. Guarded Decision Reuse activates these persistent decisions from observed receipts; Certified Callback Substitution executes them through the native interface and records removal of the registered slow callback. New semantic decisions, unsupported evidence, and selector abstention invoke the original actor again. The representation restricts what feedback may change, while complete-task measurements establish quality and cost. On HumanEval, HarnessMM preserves Codex success at 90.82\% while reducing Tokens/task (k) from 66.72 to 47.02 (29.54\% saving). For DeepSeek Harness, success rises from 71.43\% to 85.71\% while Tokens/task (k) fall from 96.28 to 11.62 (87.93\% saving). A separate MBPP ablation measures 26.91\% lower cost than single-use graphs and 19.52\% lower cost than retained callbacks. These results establish guarded decision reuse as a practical way to reduce repeated reasoning in existing harnesses.

papers.title: Exploiting the Weyl-Chamber Structure for Hardware-Aware Quantum Circuit Compression
papers.summary: Quantum circuit compression based on tensor networks enables long-time simulation of quantum many-body dynamics on near-term hardware. While Riemannian optimization has been successfully employed for this purpose, it typically optimizes over the manifold of generic two-qubit unitaries. Consequently, the resulting gates must still be synthesized into the hardware's native gate set via KAK decomposition, an overhead that partially negates the original compression gain. We show that Riemannian-optimized gates already exhibit a predictable Weyl structure: near-$R_{ZZ}$ for the Ising model and near-fSim for the Heisenberg XXZ model. Building on this insight, we investigate whether parameterized optimization directly over the native gate set can offer a beneficial trade-off between expressivity and circuit efficiency by reducing the circuit's dimensionality. When comparing the two approaches, we find that the small residual Weyl parameters neglected by the latter are essential for high compression of the Ising propagator, whereas for the Heisenberg propagator, the native XXZ structure can be exploited directly to build a more efficient compressed circuit.

papers.title: U-NeXt: General-purpose event detection for neonatal EEG
papers.summary: We developed U-NeXt, a general framework for neonatal electroencephalography (EEG) event detection based on semantic segmentation. Its convolutional encoder-decoder directly segments individual channels using long input segments to preserve temporal context. A shared architecture and training framework were developed using low-voltage interval, artefact, and seizure datasets containing 51, 98, and 278 neonates, respectively, comprising over 11,000 hours of EEG and 82,000 annotated events. Performance was compared with task-specific ConvNeXt classifiers. For seizure detection, we also evaluated U-NeXt+, trained on an expanded dataset. Both U-NeXt variants and the ConvNeXt baseline were evaluated on two independent held-out seizure datasets, Helsinki and Cork, comprising 130 neonates, with recordings annotated by three experts. U-NeXt improved detection across all three event types, with particular gains in sensitivity for short events. U-NeXt+ achieved Matthews correlation coefficients of 0.862 and 0.891 on Helsinki and Cork, respectively, and improved hourly seizure burden correlations by 30-40% relative to ConvNeXt. U-NeXt+ met the criterion for expert-level performance on both datasets (p < 0.001). In separate computational benchmarks, U-NeXt reduced batch inference time relative to ConvNeXt by 254-fold on a central processing unit and 200-fold on a graphics processing unit. A common segmentation framework improves detection across diverse neonatal EEG event types while substantially reducing inference time. Accurate seizure burden estimates and performance comparable to expert reviewers support its potential use in continuous monitoring and clinical decision support.

papers.title: Numerical analysis of a Lax-Wendroff type lattice Boltzmann scheme for the advection equation
papers.summary: A linear monodimensional lattice Boltzmann scheme with three velocities tackling the advection equation is investigated. We prove that it is second-order accurate and provide necessary and sufficient stability conditions through an explicit formula involving the two relaxation parameters. Relying on existing results for finite difference schemes, we prove convergence for smooth initial data with initialization of the non-conserved moments at equilibrium. Several numerical simulations illustrate these theoretical findings.

papers.title: Joint Angular-Power Distributions of Interfering Nanohertz Gravitational Waves
papers.summary: Finite populations of supermassive black-hole binaries produce fluctuations in both gravitational-wave power and pulsar timing correlations. We characterize the realization-dependent, orientation-averaged Earth-term angular correlation through its frequency-resolved Legendre coefficients. A hybrid model of bright sources and a Gaussian faint background extends the conditional Gamma distribution in the many-weak-source limit to non-central $χ^2$ statistics, yielding correlated multipoles after population marginalization. Our analytical variance decomposition and SMBHB population simulations reveal a population-dependent transition from interference dominated variance at low frequencies to population-power-dominated variance at high frequencies. In the many-weak-source regime, a multivariate lognormal approximation captures the main features of the joint distribution using only the first two log-cumulants. These results provide statistical benchmarks for fluctuations in both the overall amplitude and angular structure of the realized correlation.
papers.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures; 7 pages of Supplemental Material with 1 figure

papers.title: Homogenization of the Stokes equations in a domain perforated by a thin truss
papers.summary: We consider the homogenization problem of the stationary Stokes equations in a periodically perforated domain whose solid structure consists of a thin truss. That is, the width $a_ε$ of the truss tends to zero faster than the period size $ε$. We identify the different scaling regimes and derive the corresponding effective equations. In the critical regime, we obtain the Brinkman equations, while in the subcritical regime, we recover the unchanged Stokes equations. In a subrange of the supercritical regime, we derive Darcy's law as the effective equation. Furthermore, we explicitly compute the effective coefficients in the Darcy and Brinkman limits. Moreover, as a tool in the analysis, we establish the analogous homogenization result for a periodic forest of cylinders. Finally, we also consider the homogenization result for a fence of cylinders.
papers.comment: 66 pages, 12 figures, Keywords: Homogenization, connected structures, Stokes-Brinkman-Darcy limits

papers.title: Quantum Cadence: Post-Quantum Consensus with Multiple Concurrent Proposers
papers.summary: The consensus protocols of most high-performance blockchains use quorum certificates, which bundle the signatures of a quorum of validators. Signature schemes such as BLS can aggregate the signatures of a whole quorum into a single short signature, which keeps these certificates small. A large-scale quantum computer would break these schemes, and no post-quantum scheme with comparable aggregate size and aggregation time is known. Without aggregation, a certificate holds one large post-quantum signature per member of the quorum, so it becomes infeasible for each validator to broadcast certificates, as modern consensus protocols often require. We present Quantum Cadence, a post-quantum consensus protocol with multiple concurrent proposers that avoids certificates altogether: every validator counts quorums among the messages it has received itself. Its safety and liveness do not even depend on signatures, although we add signatures to obtain accountability. Quantum Cadence builds on Cadence and replaces its slot consensus, Chorus, with Quantum Chorus, which keeps the optimal fast-path latency of Chorus: dissemination followed by two rounds of votes. When its fast path fails, Quantum Chorus runs Coda, our signature-free Byzantine agreement for multiple proposers. We also outline how the Conductor, which schedules the slots of Cadence, can be adapted to Quantum Cadence. In simulations with 200 validators, Quantum Chorus has a latency comparable to that of Chorus and scales better with the number of proposers.

papers.title: Frontier-OPD: Discovering the Edge of Agent Capability and Teaching Agents to Go Beyond
papers.summary: On-policy distillation aligns teacher feedback with a student's current behavior, yet acquiring useful supervision for multi-turn agents requires identifying both where guidance is needed and whether the student can sustain the interaction afterward. We introduce Frontier-OPD, which addresses this problem through the student's learning frontier: decision situations that remain challenging but admit useful autonomous continuation after brief teacher guidance. To operationalize this frontier, Frontier-OPD organizes on-policy experience into a shared-state trajectory graph, where trajectory-balanced aggregation of teacher-student disagreement identifies distinct intervention candidates while preserving the histories needed for replay. Short teacher bridges are then assessed by comparing agreement over the bridge and the ensuing student continuation with an equally long segment of the original trajectory, providing a behavioral proxy for guidance that the current student can build on. Accepted teacher responses augment ordinary distillation data, and fresh rollouts renew the frontier estimate as the policy changes. Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and ScienceWorld report higher mean autonomous performance than the compared distillation baselines across the evaluated student scales and teacher configurations, with ablations indicating complementary effects of candidate selection and guidance filtering. In one ALFWorld timing setting, the additional collection cost is offset by a shorter time to a target success rate.

papers.title: Multiplicative vs. Additive State Coupling in Learned Optimizer Schedules
papers.summary: We learn schedules for a continuous penalty relaxation of MAX-CUT by backpropagating through an unrolled classical solver. A state-blind schedule generalizes to instances substantially larger than those used for training. A state-adaptive bilinear schedule also generalizes out of distribution, outperforming its untrained baseline across 15 seeds ($t=4.1$). By contrast, an additive ablation with identical inputs and output heads is statistically indistinguishable from the bilinear model in distribution but performs worse than its own baseline out of distribution ($t=-11.7$). This separation appears without regularization and persists across a $30$ round weight-decay sweep: the bilinear advantage remains significant at every tested value, whereas the additive model never recovers. The results in this setting isolate how solver state enters the schedule, rather than state adaptivity alone, as the architectural distinction associated with out-of-distribution transfer.

papers.title: CompMVR: Compression-Aware Multi-View Restoration Using Diffusion Models for Geometrically Consistent 3D Reconstruction
papers.summary: Real-world 3D reconstruction pipelines often rely on multi-view images degraded by lossy compression. While compression artifacts have been extensively studied in single-image or video restoration, their impact on multi-view geometry remains largely overlooked. In this work, we identify compression-induced cross-view geometric inconsistency as a critical failure mode, where view-dependent artifacts disrupt feature matching, dense correspondence, camera parameter estimation, and downstream 3D reconstruction tasks such as novel view synthesis. To address this problem, we propose CompMVR, a compression-aware multi-view diffusion restoration framework that jointly refines compressed views while preserving cross-view consistency, and construct compressed datasets for systematic evaluation. Unlike conventional restoration methods that optimize each image independently for 2D perceptual quality, CompMVR leverages learned compression priors and cross-view correspondence to recover visual details while improving geometric reliability across views. Experiments across diverse datasets, codecs, and compression levels demonstrate gains in restoration quality and downstream 3D tasks, including novel-view synthesis, camera pose estimation, and view matching. These results establish compressed multi-view restoration as a distinct problem and highlight its importance for 3D reconstruction under lossy compression. Code and data for this paper are available at https://mchaewon.github.io/CompMVR-project-page/.

papers.title: CARES: Coverage-Aware Replay Exemplar Selection for Continual Learning
papers.summary: Replay-based Continual Learning mitigates catastrophic forgetting by keeping a buffer of past samples, making buffer composition critical under a fixed memory budget. Recent coreset-based replay methods improve buffer quality using model-derived gradients, losses, or auxiliary optimization, but incur substantial computational overhead as memory is repeatedly updated. We propose CARES, a continual model-optimization-free approach for buffer construction that instead exploits the geometry of a frozen pretrained feature space using class-aware, density-weighted coverage. We evaluate CARES across balanced, imbalanced, and label-noisy streams under online class- and task-incremental settings. On Tiny-ImageNet, CARES is 2.3 to 8.8 times faster than existing coreset-based selectors. Although CARES achieves this speedup using no training signal from the continual learner, it ranks among the state of the art across balanced, imbalanced, and label-noisy streams under online class- and task-incremental settings, outperforming the strongest baseline by up to 7.58 percentage points under class imbalance while also attaining higher average accuracy on Tiny-ImageNet. Code will be released upon publication

papers.title: Unconventional charge density wave order in ErTe$_{3}$: symmetry breakings and fluctuations probed by Raman scattering
papers.summary: Recent experiments have revealed unexpected mirror-symmetry breakings in the charge density-wave (CDW) state of rare-earth tritellurides, suggesting a putative ferro-axial CDW state. Here we report polarization-resolved Raman scattering measurements tracking the point-group symmetry breakings across the CDW phase transition in the rare-earth tritelluride ErTe$_3$. We show that the mirror-symmetry breakings follow closely the emergence of the CDW order, suggesting a single component CDW order parameter. Furthermore, Raman measurements in the $A_{2g}$ symmetry channel above the CDW transition temperature indicate the absence of significant ferro-axial fluctuations. We discuss the broad implications of these findings with respect to the nature of the CDW state in the tritellurides.
papers.comment: to appear in JPS Conference Proceedings

papers.title: ParaTaxe: a Suite of Tools for Processing and Publishing Multi-parallel Corpora
papers.summary: Over the past fifteen years, digital tools for parallelizing and aligning textual corpora have developed significantly within the field of digital humanities. Several projects and software tools have been created to compare different translations or versions of texts.
