In \textit{ab initio} trajectories of the Janus-derived sheets, Se crosses the Mo plane already at 300~K, whereas S stays in place at 300~K and the sheet reconstructs only at 900~K. With a free in-plane cell, the crossings precede an anisotropic lattice contraction, which therefore results from the structural reconstruction. Reactive MD simulations of 50~nm sheets show that, when S remains, the Mo lattice stays crystalline in nanometric domains that disappear with time and temperature, with pores/holes at 900~K. In contrast, when Se remains, the Mo lattice loses crystalline order within the first picosecond, and 36--39\% of the Se atoms cross at every temperature. In a depleted lateral MoS$_2$/MoSe$_2$ heterostructure, both modes coexist in one sheet, each half reconstructing like its single-chalcogen counterpart, suggesting chalcogen patterning as a route to define crystalline and disordered regions in a single monolayer.

papers.title: Discrete WKB approach to density profiles in inhomogeneous two-band free-fermion chains
papers.summary: We extend the discrete WKB method to one-dimensional bipartite tight-binding chains of free fermions with slowly varying hopping amplitudes and on-site potentials. We focus on the inhomogeneous Rice-Mele model, suggesting possible experimental realizations thereof in optical superlattices. We derive explicit semiclassical expressions for the single-particle wave functions and density of states, as well as the sublattice-resolved local particle densities and filling fraction at arbitrary Fermi energy. In particular, we show that the WKB density profiles agree with those obtained from the local-density approximation. We analyze the spatial dependence of the local band edges and its consequences for the global spectral structure, and clarify the role played by the phase-space topology in determining the Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization conditions. Finally, we illustrate our results with two representative examples: a homogeneous Rice-Mele chain subject to a harmonic trap and a fully inhomogeneous chain containing a domain wall.

papers.title: Are Textual Residuals Truly Complementary? Learning Visual Complements under Semantic Superposition for Visible-Infrared Person Re-Identification
papers.summary: Text-enhanced visible-infrared person re-identification (VI-ReID) exploits textual descriptions to compensate for appearance cues that are weak or unavailable under infrared imaging. Existing methods construct compensation from differences between modality-oriented textual representations, implicitly assuming that textual differences are visually complementary. We revisit this assumption through semantic superposition and show that dense textual residuals may entangle useful appearance variations with redundant, making direct residual fusion unreliable. We propose Superposition-Aware Residual Calibration, which transforms dense textual differences into selective and visually grounded complements. Low-Interference Sparse Residual Learning represents modality-oriented text embeddings as sparse activation strengths over a shared dictionary, selects positive strength differences, and suppresses both dictionary-level overlap and activation-weighted interference to reconstruct a compact, selectively controlled residual. Visual Complement and Counterfactual Calibration further calibrates the residual against identity-specific RGB-IR visual discrepancies, encouraging retained semantics to provide meaningful compensation while preserving the residual structure. Experiments on Tri-SYSU-MM01, Tri-RegDB, and Tri-LLCM show that SARC consistently improves the VI-ReID backbone and remains competitive with text-assisted methods. Mechanism analyses show that SARC produces more concentrated textual variations, reduces dictionary-level feature interference, and improves residual-visual-complement alignment for most samples. These results demonstrate that effective cross-modal compensation requires textual residuals to be selectively represented and explicitly calibrated, rather than directly treated as visual complements. Code and implementation details will be released upon publication.

papers.title: CounselPlex: A Stressor-Aware Full-Duplex Counseling Model
papers.summary: Full-duplex speech models can listen and speak at the same time, enabling natural, low-latency interaction. In counseling, however, these models often focus on the latest utterance and lose track of the seeker's underlying problem. We call this failure Stressor Blindness. We propose CounselPlex, a stressor-aware full-duplex framework that uses two operations. CounselPlex updates a short stressor state during seeker silence and injects this state into <PAD> positions while listening. We also introduce RoPE Position Shift Augmentation (RPSA), which broadens positional coverage during training and improves performance at longer turn depths in our evaluation. LLM-judge evaluations show improved counseling quality and stressor grounding over strong baselines.

papers.title: SP-Guide: Enhancing Aerial Vision-Language Navigation with Spatial Priors
papers.summary: Aerial vision-language navigation (AVLN) requires a UAV to reach a language-described target from partial egocentric observations while reasoning over large outdoor scenes. Existing approaches typically fuse view-centered RGB observations and globally anchored history maps as generic visual embeddings, leaving cross-modal spatial alignment to be learned from sparse navigation supervision. We present SP-Guide, a transformer- based goal-prediction framework that addresses this weakness of alignment through a Spatial Prior Cross-Modal Encoder, an Instruction Enhanced Decoder, and a Goal Convergence Filter for terminal target refinement. Experiments implemented on the CityNav benchmark show that SP-Guide improves success rate over the representative baselines, with the largest gains on unseen environments. These results indicate that physically grounded spatial priors provide an effective inductive bias for robust AVLN.

papers.title: Foundation Models Meet Power Grid Topology for Cascade Prediction
papers.summary: Accurate early-stage prediction of cascading failure severity is essential for assessing the vulnerability of power transmission networks. However, existing data-driven approaches often rely on network-specific representations, limiting their generalizability across power system topologies. This work investigates the complementary capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for cascading failure severity prediction. First, standalone LLM predictors are developed using a LoRA-fine-tuned LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct model with varying degrees of topological information. A hybrid Graph-LLM fusion framework is then proposed, integrating a Topology-Aware Graph Attention Transformer (TAGAT) with the LLM through confidence-gated fusion. TAGAT captures structural dependencies among transmission lines, while the LLM extracts representations from early-stage power-flow observations and aggregated cascade descriptors. The frameworks are evaluated on 30,000 simulated cascading failure scenarios for each of the IEEE 118-bus and IEEE 300-bus systems. Using only the first four cascade steps, the hybrid framework achieves weighted F1 scores of 0.94 and 0.92, respectively. In cross-system transfer from IEEE 118-bus to IEEE 300-bus, it achieves 0.72 zero-shot accuracy, improving to 0.83 with limited target-system calibration, outperforming standalone models and conventional baselines. These results show the potential of combining graph-based structural learning with foundation models to improve cascading failure severity prediction and cross-system transferability.

papers.title: Elementary proofs of quantum lower bounds for element distinctness and k-sum
papers.summary: We give elementary proofs of the $Ω(n^{2/3})$ quantum query lower bound for element distinctness and the $Ω(n^{k/(k+1)})$ lower bound for the $k$-sum problem, for fixed $k$ and sufficiently large groups. The proofs use only basic properties of quantum states and linear algebra, analyzing the differences of algorithm states on different inputs.

papers.title: First-Order Structure of the Linearised Einstein Equations: Constant-Curvature Backgrounds
papers.summary: Teukolsky's decoupled equations and Wald's adjoint method of metric reconstruction are built from second-order operators: the linearised Einstein operator G, the curvature-extraction operator T, the decoupled operator O and the reconstruction operator S^*, related by SG=OT. We show that on four-dimensional constant-curvature backgrounds with non-zero Lambda all of these operators factor into first-order maps through a single intermediate variable: the perturbation of the self-dual half of the spin connection. We also show that for non-zero Lambda the metric perturbation is itself obtained from the connection perturbation by a first-order map. The connection therefore gives a complete description of linearised gravity, and the fourth-order identity SG=OT follows by composition from a single second-order identity. Using conformal flatness, we choose the Hertz-potential map so that, after a conformal rescaling, the potential obeys the flat wave equation component by component. This leads to a new reconstruction scheme, in which the potential is sourced by the curvature psi, which in turn obeys a decoupled sourced equation. A prescribed curvature is then reached by a second-order rather than a fourth-order equation, and the corrector is local and algebraic in the stress-energy tensor. The price is that the full curvature, rather than a single component, must be determined, and that the reality of the reconstructed metric becomes a condition, which we argue holds for retarded solutions. We illustrate the scheme for a static point mass in de Sitter space, where it gives a real metric perturbation that agrees with linearised Schwarzschild-de Sitter up to a diffeomorphism. We view these results as a proof of concept for a first-order Teukolsky-Wald framework on Kerr.

papers.title: Natural Language Autoencoders Identify Without Explaining
papers.summary: Natural Language Autoencoders (NLAs) express a model's internal activations in the form of readable text. The verbalizer turns an activation into an English explanation; the reconstructor then converts that explanation back into an activation, and the explanation is considered successful if the round trip brings back the original activation. We claim that this criterion evaluates whether the information is sufficient and does not address descriptive faithfulness. A sentence can contain sufficient information to make it possible to identify an activation even if it wrongly explains what the activation does: in the case of reconstruction, the primary aim is to accurately identify the activations and not to describe them. This issue has the same structure as the chain-of-thought faithfulness problem, in which verbal output that has been trained to go with a process is taken as a report on that process, and it parallels the dissociation between an individual's introspective report and the actual governing process as documented in human psychology. Although proposed as interpretability tools for the purpose of alignment, NLAs reintroduce, through unverified explanations, the epistemic problem that they were intended to resolve.

papers.title: Developing Security Metrics for Automated Compliance Checking
papers.summary: To automatically check for compliance with security-related standards, prose requirements must be translated to technical properties to make them measurable. A multitude of metrics have been proposed in past literature, but they are lacking a systematic methodology for their elicitation. Without such a methodology, metrics remain inconsistent in their data models and abstraction levels, they exhibit considerable overlaps and are difficult to combine to comprehensively cover a standard's requirement. In this paper, we develop a data model for security metrics based on a systematization of compliance requirements, and we propose a methodology for their elicitation. The method is based on an ontology that enables a systematic development of metrics with a comparable degree of abstraction. We also present our initial work on an open-source effort that demonstrates that our approach also supports a collaborative development of metrics.
papers.comment: 15 pages, 1 figure, 1 table. Author-accepted manuscript of a paper published in the proceedings of IFIP SEC 2026. The final authenticated version is available from Springer Nature at https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-032-27993-4_20
papers.journal: In: Proceedings of IFIP SEC 2026, IFIP Advances in Information and Communication Technology, Springer, 2026

papers.title: The Dst index - empirical fits and temporal correlations
papers.summary: Here I show how it is possible to make an empirical fit of yearly sets of Dst index values to the log-normal distribution, using the Kullback-Liebler divergence to test each fit performance. Further, since any real sequence of Dst values contains correlation with the near-past, I also compute autocorrelations in order to understand the timescales over which it retains memory.
papers.comment: 9 pages. No AI was used in the preparation of this manuscript

papers.title: Conditional Neural Processes for Self-Supervised Goal Discovery in Action Imitation
papers.summary: Inspired by infants' ability to learn novel tasks by imitating others, in this work we evaluate to what extent Conditional Neural Processes can autonomously learn representations of actions that are informative about their underlying goal. We show that the addition of an attention mechanism in the hidden space fosters the emergence of robust goal representations early on in the observation of an action sequence, making it a promising model for a robotic self-supervised general learner.
papers.comment: Presented at the poster session of the Workshop on World Models and Predictive Coding in Cognitive Robotics @ IROS2023 (https://world-model.emergent-symbol.systems/)

papers.title: Identity Amortization: Shared Resources and the Cost of Sybil Attacks
papers.summary: Sybil defenses commonly price identities by requiring a resource for each one. When one resource can support several identities, an adversary can pay less per identity than the defense intends. We call this identity amortization: a strict reduction in the minimum cost of provisioning identities when resources may be shared, relative to provisioning each one independently. It is a second route to the gap that a Sybil attack exploits. When influence is assigned per identity, a defense calibrated to the nominal price can overestimate the cost of a Sybil threshold by up to the number of identities one resource supports. For any resource catalogue, we give exact tests for when identity amortization occurs, where it begins, and its largest error; a sharing cap below the onset removes it. Because the tests need only prices and capacities, they apply to any defense that admits identities against a shareable resource, telling designers whether the assumed per-identity cost is paid, how wrong it can be, and which intervention restores it most cheaply for honest participants. On published phone-verification prices, per-account estimates overstate provisioning cost 1.6 to 4.3 times; Tor's raised per-address relay limit cut modeled attack cost by 8 to 72%, depending on the address-to-relay price ratio.

papers.title: Stochastic and quantum autonomous information machine: efficiency fluctuations, precision and optimization
papers.summary: We investigate the conversion between thermal and informational resources in an autonomous machine coupled to thermal reservoirs and a tape, playing the role of an information reservoir. The machine is able to perform information erasure driven by heat, and information-powered refrigeration, for which we introduce suitable efficiency definitions. We focus on the role of fluctuations in the currents and stochastic efficiencies, as well as in operation at optimal performance. The model is also extended to allow a coherent information reservoir, which is able to modify operation and performance. All in all, our work provides insights for the design and optimization of information-to-work conversion devices at small scales.

papers.title: Automated Fetal Magnetocardiography Reconstruction Using a Biophysical Forward Model
papers.summary: Objective: Fetal magnetocardiography (fMCG) enables early detection of cardiac disease by non-invasively measuring fetal electrophysiological activity. However, current signal estimation methods for fMCG require complex, labor-intensive human processing because they rely on blind source separation or template-based projection techniques. Methods: We propose an automated signal reconstruction approach that recovers fetal and maternal cardiac activity from fMCG measurements without manual annotation. Our approach leverages the relationship between measurements and cardiac signals via a biophysically grounded forward model that represents cardiac sources as time-varying magnetic dipoles. This enables reconstruction of physiologically interpretable three-dimensional vectorcardiographic signals along with their spatial position. Results: Validation on synthetic data with known ground truth confirms accurate recovery of cardiac source parameters. On real fMCG recordings, the reconstruction shows strong agreement with established reference methods. Conclusion: The proposed forward-model approach automatically reconstructs fetal and maternal cardiac activity from fMCG recordings and produces signals in an interpretable vectorcardiographic source domain. Significance: Automated, interpretable fMCG reconstruction could make fetal cardiac assessment more reliable and support potential translation into prenatal care.
papers.comment: 29 pages, 16 figures. Includes supplementary material. Published in IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering. Code: https://github.com/MLI-lab/fetal_magnetocardiography

papers.title: Optimal Random Taxation
papers.summary: We consider the Ramsey problem of optimal government policy and give examples where lotteries are essential for the optimal solution. When markets are complete and the representative agent's coefficient of relative prudence is bounded, lotteries are typically not optimal. For the incomplete markets case, we prove analytically that lotteries improve welfare for some calibrations with CRRA utility, and we give a simple numerical example for this claim. When the agent's coefficient of relative risk aversion is unbounded for small consumption, lotteries typically improve welfare and can be used to approximate the first-best solution arbitrarily well in both the complete and the incomplete markets cases. However, in the complete markets case, when debt constraints are not too tight and the representative agent is sufficiently patient, lotteries can be purified in the sense that there is a deterministic solution that gives the same value.

papers.title: When is more search useful? An Empirical Study of Search Utility in Quality-Aware Decoding for Machine Translation
papers.summary: Quality-Aware Decoding (QAD) improves machine translation through test-time scaling, generating multiple candidate translations and selecting the final output with a quality-aware decoder. Usually the same candidate budget N is spent on every source sentence, assuming that all inputs require the same amount of search. We show that this assumption does not hold and that the quality gain obtained from additional candidates varies across sentences. We study search utility through three quantities: total scaling gain, how much quality a sentence can gain from a much larger candidate pool; marginal scaling gain, the expected gain from generating one additional batch of candidates; and the sampling saturation point, the candidate budget required to realize most of the total scaling gain. We investigate two sources of information for predicting these quantities: signals available before candidate-set expansion, and statistics computed from the candidate pool accumulated during search. We find that sentence-level signals correlate with total scaling gain but are less informative about the sampling saturation point. In contrast, properties of the current candidate pool provide useful signals of marginal scaling gain. Finally, we show that these signals can identify sentences that obtain larger gains when additional search is selectively applied.

papers.title: Retiming Robot Demonstrations with a Learned Speed Prior
papers.summary: The pace of a robot demonstration is often determined by the teleoperator rather than by the task itself. As a result, the same motion can appear at widely different speeds across demonstrations, and policies trained on such data may inherit operator-specific timing along with task behavior. We propose to learn a speed prior directly from large-scale demonstration data. Given a task instruction, a motion path and the images along it, it predicts a distribution over execution speed along the path, from which a chosen quantile defines a consistent clock for retiming each demonstration. Existing methods derive the acceleration signal from the very data they accelerate, so each new task costs another fit, annotation, or pair of predefined rates. A single trained speed prior instead covers every task in a corpus. We fit a speed prior on both robot teleoperation data and handheld demonstrations in which a human arm, rather than a robot arm, moves the gripper, and use it to retime robot demonstrations to the handheld pace before fine-tuning a vision-language-action policy. For execution, we pair the policy with a real-time optimal-control layer that tracks predicted action chunks under robot constraints using the predicted pace. On 120 RoboLab tasks, policies fine-tuned on our learned clocks succeed more often and move with up to half the jerk compared with policies fine-tuned on the original demonstration timing and uniformly accelerated to the same speed. On a real robot, our policy stacks cups in 3.50s, 1.72$\times$ faster than the default policy's 6.02s while succeeding as often, in 29 of 30 trials. Videos and further material are available at https://mllab.snu.ac.kr/projects/learned_speed_prior.

papers.title: Entanglement entropy of evolving wormholes
papers.summary: We compute the entanglement entropy of a discretized scalar field in the fixed spacetime background of an evolving wormhole. Evolving wormholes are a class of time dependent and spherically symmetric wormhole geometries. In both expanding and contracting models, we find dynamically generated entanglement. Asymptotically far from the wormhole throat, the entanglement entropy is well described by the leading term in the area law, although its coefficient can depend sensitively on the value of the UV cutoff. As the UV cutoff is decreased, the coefficient becomes progressively less sensitive to the cutoff, providing numerical evidence that it approaches a cutoff-independent value in the continuum limit. Near the throat, we find a double-dip structure in the entanglement entropy which cannot be described by the leading and logarithmic contributions to the area law.

papers.title: EMG Tokenization Preserves Movement Information at a Fraction of the Bitrate
papers.summary: Wireless electromyography (EMG) interfaces must balance electrode coverage against transmission bandwidth. Here, we show that compact EMG tokens substantially reduce payload while retaining information for three-dimensional hand-pose decoding. We evaluate two causal tokenizers fitted without pose labels: an encoder pretrained to reconstruct EMG spectra and one based on SPAR, an engineered spectral-spatial representation of neighbouring electrodes. In personalized, within-session experiments with 320-channel EMG from nine participants, we compare tokenized and continuous features using matched decoder architectures and training procedures. Averaged across decoders, tokenization changed mean error by +0.01 mm for SPAR (95% confidence interval: -0.12 to 0.14) and +0.45 mm for the learned representation (0.10 to 0.82). Both increases met a 1 mm non-inferiority criterion. Stored token arrays reduced payloads 41-fold relative to raw EMG and 36-fold relative to continuous SPAR features. On sampled windows of the public emg2pose benchmark's test partition, absolute differences in mean error between learned tokens and continuous features were below 0.05 mm across 176 participants and in the subset of 20 participants unseen during training. Electrode coverage, calibration, and unseen recordings affected SPAR decoding more than quantization did. In a computational benchmark, optimized SPAR generated tokens for 63 channels within 20 ms on a Cortex-M55 microcontroller. These findings support tokenization as a compact interface between wearable sensing and movement decoding, allowing decoders to be updated while the wearable encoder and transmitted representation remain fixed.
papers.comment: 11 pages, 7 figures; 12-page supplement included. Supplementary Data 1-9 (CSV) are provided as ancillary files

papers.title: Systematic Study of Neutrino-Nucleus Interactions for the DUNE Experiment
papers.summary: The recent generation of high-precision neutrino oscillation experiments, such as the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE), relies on the accurate reconstruction of incident neutrino energy to determine fundamental parameters like Charge-Parity (CP) violation and the neutrino mass hierarchy. The use of Liquid Argon, introduces significant theoretical complexities. This dissertation provides a investigation into neutrino-nucleus scattering phenomenologies, connecting fundamental electroweak theory with computational simulations using the GENIE Monte Carlo event generator. The study evaluates the limitations of traditional frameworks, such as the Relativistic Fermi Gas (RFG) model, specifically addressing the Axial Mass parameter and its impact on the Charged Current Quasi-Elastic (CCQE) channel. By comparing baseline RFG predictions against experimental data from MicroBooNE, this research quantifies the necessity of advanced many-body nuclear frameworks. The implementation of the Local Fermi Gas (LFG) model, Random Phase Approximation (RPA) screening, and the SuperScaling Approximation (SuSAv2) are systematically analyzed to resolve kinematic biases. Additionally, the impact of modernized phenomenological constraints, including the updated $M_A^{RES} = 0.96$ GeV for resonant pion production and the 2021 Bodek-Yang parameter updates for Deep Inelastic Scattering (DIS), is evaluated. Furthermore, this research integrates university extension initiatives by developing and presenting macroscopic 3D-printed educational models, consisting of a Linear Accelerator (LINAC) analog and a scattering experiment, and finally presenting it into the festival "Mais Ciência Por Favor".

papers.title: Sensitivity-Guided Parameter Estimation of Bubbly Liquid via a Nonlinear Wave Equation and Physics-InformedNeuralNetworks
papers.summary: Interactions between ultrasound and microbubbles underlie a range of biomedical and industrial applications, yet predicting how the physical parameters of the medium and bubbles govern nonlinear wave propagation remains difficult. This study proposes a parameter estimation framework that combines a Korteweg-de Vries-Burgers (KdVB) equation, describing weakly nonlinear wave propagation in a bubbly liquid, with a physics-informed neural network (PINN). The contributions are threefold. First, the PINN reproduces the reference solution of the governing equation in the forward problem, with a near-zero prediction error at the initial time that confirms the initial condition is enforced exactly as intended. Second, prior to inverse estimation, a sensitivity analysis is introduced that quantifies, at both the coefficient and solution levels, how each of eight physical parameters influences the KdVB equation, allowing the expected difficulty of estimating each parameter to be assessed in advance. Third, based on this assessment, single-parameter inverse estimation is performed for seven of the eight parameters using the PINN. Liquid viscosity, bubble initial radius, liquid density, sound speed, and liquid pressure are estimated with errors of 0.8-2.1%, the polytropic exponent converges only partially, and the surface tension coefficient cannot be estimated at all, consistent with the sensitivity analysis. These results establish a general framework for identifying and estimating the physical parameters governing nonlinear wave propagation in bubbly liquids from observed waveform data.

papers.title: Anisotropic flow measurements in OO and Ne-Ne collisions with ALICE
papers.summary: The LHC results have demonstrated that small collision systems can exhibit collective behavior reminiscent of that~observed in heavy-ion collisions, opening a new frontier for exploring the connection between nuclear structure and collective dynamics at ultra-relativistic energies. However, the interpretation of collectivity in small collision systems is limited by understanding the proton subnucleonic structure. The ${}^{16}$O and ${}^{20}$Ne collisions delivered by the LHC offer an opportunity to study the influence of nuclear geometry on anisotropic flow in systems where the nuclear structure is well-constrained. In this proceeding, measurements of the anisotropic flow of charged particles, $v_n$, in OO and Ne-Ne collisions involving up to eight-particle correlations are presented, using the multi-particle cumulant method. Furthermore, the first reconstruction of the probability distribution function of elliptic flow $P(v_2)$, and the first measurement of the ratio $v_3\{4\}/v_3\{2\}$ in light-ion collision systems are reported. These measurements provide deeper insight into the role of nuclear geometry-driven flow in light-ion collisions.
papers.comment: 4 pages, 6 figures, Proceedings of the 22nd International Conference on Strangeness in Quark Matter (SQM2026)
papers.journal: Journal of Subatomic Particles and Cosmology 6, 100558 (2026)

papers.title: Robust Offset-Free Lane-Keeping Control Framework for Vision-Only Automated Vehicles
papers.summary: Achieving accurate, real-time lane-keeping control during high-speed cornering on large-curvature roads while ensuring robust vehicle stability is a critical challenge in autonomous driving. To address this challenge, this study developed a robust offset-free model predictive control (OF-MPC) framework for vision-based autonomous vehicle lane-keeping. The regulation problem in this framework is solved using several algorithms. Numerical simulation results indicated that the interpolation-tube-based constrained iterative linear quadratic regulator (itube-CILQR) algorithm outperformed solvers based on the standard Interior Point Optimizer (IPOPT) and Operator Splitting Quadratic Program (OSQP), achieving a mean computation time of less than 5 ms. The itube-CILQR algorithm was then used for vehicle control in vision-based lane-keeping experiments in a simulation environment to quantify the perceptual uncertainty of a visual perception model (multitask UNet). This quantification was performed using the OF-MPC framework for traffic scenes that were not encountered during model training. Overall, the developed OF-MPC framework and the proposed method for characterizing the perceptual uncertainty of a visual perception system in unseen environments can contribute to the future development of advanced autonomous driving systems.

papers.title: The Answer Knows Where to Look: Zooming before MLLMs Answer under Visual-Token Budgets
papers.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) read images through visual tokens, and under the small per-image budgets that efficient deployment requires, the fine text of documents, charts and infographics becomes illegible. Zooming in recovers the evidence, but the region must be chosen before the model answers. We find that MLLMs know where the evidence is, but not in a form that can be read before they answer: the answer tokens localize it from the middle layers on, whereas the attention available before answering does so only in the top layers, at a depth that varies across models, and diffusely. Supervising the pre-answer attention to point degrades reading, and the benefit of zooming is governed by each image's information gap. Building on these findings, we introduce ours, which lets an MLLM look where its answer would. A dedicated look token, processed in a single prefill and kept out of the answering pass, learns in hindsight to attend as the model's own correct answers do, extracting this knowledge into a concentrated pointer before any answer exists. Its hidden state then selects how to look, from no zoom to crops, square windows, windows that adapt to the pointer and foveated warps, supervised by the counterfactual outcome of every view. ours needs no box annotations, per-model layer search, external localizers or generation before the answer. On Qwen3-VL at three scales and five text-rich benchmarks, it surpasses the strongest baseline by 4.8-9.1 points at 98 visual tokens per view and attention-guided zooming by 11.1-17.0 points, while running faster than attention-guided and grounding-based zooming.

papers.title: SemGeo-Gen: Unsupervised Generation of Approximate Cross-Instance Semantic-Geometric Correspondences
papers.summary: We introduce SemGeo-Gen, an unsupervised method for generating approximate cross-instance semantic-geometric supervision from weakly aligned 3D object collections. Our goal is not to recover exact point-level correspondences, which are often ambiguous across different instances and would require expensive, impractical manual supervision at scale. Instead, we automatically produce approximate correspondences that are semantically meaningful, geometrically consistent, and diverse enough to train modern correspondence models. Given only coarse category-level rotation alignment, SemGeo-Gen lifts multi-view DINOv2 features to 3D, aligns object instances using continuous piecewise-affine registration, and prunes candidate matches using semantic consistency. The resulting 3D correspondences can be projected into rendered views, yielding scalable 3D-3D, 3D-2D, and 2D-2D supervision without manual annotation. We validate the generated correspondences against sparse human annotations from KeypointNet, obtaining 93% PCK@0.10 and 97% PCK@0.15. More importantly, we show that using the generated correspondences for synthetic pretraining improves recent state-of-the-art semantic correspondence models on SPair-71k after fine-tuning on real data, with gains of up to 5 PCK@0.10 points. Together, these results indicate that approximate semantic-geometric supervision generated from 3D assets can improve real-image correspondence learning and serve as a scalable alternative to costly manual annotation. Project page: https://bgu-cs-vil.github.io/SemGeo-Gen/.

papers.title: Iterative Behavioral Identification for Covert Misappropriation Attacks
papers.summary: We present a data-driven, three-phase framework for covert misappropriation attacks on closed-loop networked control systems. A man-in-the-middle (MITM) adversary, with access only to intercepted input-output data, incrementally identifies the plant's behavioral subspace while maintaining stealth under an infinity-norm intrusion-detection system (IDS). Phase 1 collects an initial rank-deficient Hankel matrix using a low-amplitude probing signal that satisfies an analytical stealth bound. Phase 2 adapts online rank-increasing experiment design to the closed-loop setting, using causal predictor-based masking to limit IDS residuals while the Hankel rank grows from 1 to the full behavioral rank n + mL in exactly n + mL - 1 steps. We show that the identified subspaces are strictly nested and that the projection error of any desired trajectory decreases monotonically, strictly so almost surely at each rank increase. Phase 3 employs the final Hankel matrix in a DeePC-style optimization to synthesize a covert attack that tracks an arbitrary reference while respecting the IDS constraint. Simulations on a DC motor with PI control demonstrate full-rank identification and stealthy tracking. Stealth is guaranteed analytically in Phases 1 and 3 and is numerically supported in Phase 2. The method is model-free and assumes noise-free LTI dynamics.
papers.comment: Presented at the 17th APCA International Conference on Automatic Control and Soft Computing (CONTROLO 2026), Coimbra, Portugal, September 9-11, 2026

papers.title: AquaSense-ICS: A Hybrid Real-Simulated Cyber-Physical Dataset and Leakage-Aware Benchmark for Smart Water Quality Monitoring and Attack Detection
papers.summary: Machine-learning research on water cyber-physical systems (CPS) is constrained by datasets that are either real but chemically poor, or simulated but free of sensing noise and attacks. We present AquaSense-ICS, an open dataset and benchmark that co-registers (i) a 25.4 h recording window (8.0 h of recorded data, 26% coverage) from a Raspberry Pi 5 edge node (TDS probe and BME680 ambient sensor, 1-2 s sampling, 23,688 records), with (ii) a looped network of 13 nodes (10 junctions, 2 reservoirs, 1 tank) simulated in EPANET-MSX for six water-quality species, (iii) a parameterised library of cyber-attacks (false data injection, replay, denial of service, drift) and unintentional sensor faults with sample-level ground truth, and (iv) augmented and TimeGAN-generated sequences, flagged by an origin column. The attack, fault and water-quality labels are traceable to a seeded generator, a documented rule or a simulation input. We show that the most common way of benchmarking such hybrid data, random row splits and labels computed from the input features, yields near-perfect but uninformative scores (macro-F1 = 0.9998 for Random Forest), and we replace it with a leakage-aware protocol using chronological splits and held-out attack types rather than label reconstruction. Under this protocol, no model exceeds the constant "normal" predictor for attack classification (macro-F1 = 0.465), and the best detectors reach a mean AUROC of 0.64 on attack types unseen during training (0.35-0.93 depending on the type), leaving substantial headroom. Data and simulation files are released under CC BY 4.0 at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23390541, and attack generators and benchmark code under MIT.

papers.title: An Invitation to Algebraic Methods in Quantum Theory
papers.summary: In this paper, we present various well-studied examples of quantum systems, and discuss how they might be analysed algebraically. We analyse the harmonic oscillator, hydrogenic atom, optical components, and particle spin using multiple algebraic methods, and highlight the central importance of algebraic relationships between operators in determining the physical character of the system. In particular, we show: the ubiquity of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{so}(2,1)\cong\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$ as the ``spectrum generating algebra''; the role of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$ in determining the action of optical components; that an elementary algebraic approach to particle spin offers novel insights into its nature versus the usual approaches; and how understanding the full (often hidden) symmetry of a problem enables it to be solved immediately without the need to solve differential equations. We hope this work will serve as a gentle introduction to algebraic methods in quantum mechanics for the interested reader --- we therefore signpost active areas of research within the community.

papers.title: Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering Simulation Using GENIE Event Generator
papers.summary: The Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE) relies on the precise reconstruction of incident neutrino energy to extract oscillation parameters. The use of Liquid Argon introduces significant theoretical complexities due to nuclear effects. This work evaluates neutrino-nucleus scattering models using the GENIE Monte Carlo event generator. We demonstrate the limitations of the Relativistic Fermi Gas (RFG) model in the Charged Current Quasi-Elastic (CCQE) channel and its reliance on an inflated Axial Mass to match experimental data from MicroBooNE. We show that transitioning to advanced many-body frameworks, specifically the Local Fermi Gas (LFG) supplemented with Random Phase Approximation (RPA), is needed. Additionally, we evaluate the impact of the 2021 Bodek-Yang parameter updates on Deep Inelastic Scattering (DIS), concluding that modernized constraints are a prerequisite for mitigating systematic biases in DUNE.

papers.title: Defects in Topological Symmetric Orbifolds and their String Dual
papers.summary: We review defect topological field theories with finite gauge groups. We then concentrate on restriction and induction defects between symmetric orbifold theories and recall that the defects form an algebra. This requires identifying the features of restriction and induction defects that are independent of the order of the symmetric group, which is natural in a grand canonical framework. The construction leads to Khovanov's categorification of the Heisenberg algebra. The bulk algebra of partial permutations corresponds to the endomorphisms of the identity defect in the category. We also interpret the Hurwitz theory defects in the dual Gromov-Witten theory. This gives a defect descendant interpretation to higher level operators that arise in the integrable hierarchy of the Gromov-Witten theory of curves. In further applications, we relate known defects to our symmetric group theoretic description. For seamed surfaces, we determine the boundary operator algebra for higher values of the covering degree n and provide asymptotics for the large n growth of the number of boundary operators.

papers.title: Computational imaging through turbid, bubbly and flowing water near the telescope
papers.summary: Cameras in the surf zone or behind ship wakes look through turbid, bubbly, moving water close to the lens, yet restoration networks are usually scored only on displayed images. We introduce a measured dataset of a telescope viewing displayed images and physical objects through a 25~mm water layer 45~mm in front of its objective, under seven combinations of flow, bubbles and turbidity, with clear-water recordings as a second reference. Because the suspension scatters light far outside the 1.3\textdegree{} field of view, turbidity mainly removes contrast, 4.4- to 4.8-fold on a Siemens star. Restoring the mean of eight frames improves structural similarity (SSIM) by 0.032 over a single frame, and learned fusion of the frames adds little. One raw frame supports five-category recognition (96.8\%) as well as restored images. Adding synthetic training pairs leaves display-image scores unchanged but raises the correlation of a restored Siemens star with its clear-water recording from below 0.5 to above 0.9. These networks also improve ordinary underwater photographs without retraining, where training on measured pairs alone fails. Scoring against the digital source or a clear-water recording reverses the ranking of raw and restored images. These results support a simple pipeline: average the frames, classify raw frames directly, and restore with networks trained on measured and synthetic pairs.

papers.title: Monte Carlo-Based Indoor UAV Localization in Dynamic Environments Using Only Four Onboard Range Sensors
papers.summary: Indoor UAV localization with minimal onboard sensing remains challenging, particularly in dynamic environments. We propose augmented filtered Monte Carlo localization (AF-MCL) for 2D localization using only four single-point range sensors and measured heading. AF-MCL rejects range measurements inconsistent with the known static map and adaptively injects particles to recover from localization divergence and kidnapping. Beam classification is performed only at the previous position estimate, making its ray-casting cost independent of the particle count. The particle distribution additionally provides an online measure of localization uncertainty. Real-world experiments in a 2.10x1.63 m environment yield mean position errors of 6.4-7.7 cm under static and dynamic conditions. Simulations in 6x6 m and 10x10 m environments yield 4.5-5.2 cm mean errors; under dynamic obstacles, standard MCL reaches 12.3 cm and reliable MCL 7.7 cm. The results show that robust indoor localization under dynamic obstacles is achievable with only four single-point range measurements and heading.

papers.title: High-quality, deep formation and identification of oxygen-vacancy defects in silicon carbide
papers.summary: Optically addressable paramagnetic defects in silicon carbide (SiC) are attractive for scalable quantum technologies such as quantum sensing. PL5, PL6, and PL7 are promising defects for their high brightness and spin-readout contrast. Although generation by oxygen implantation has been reported very recently, nonuniform spin and optical properties and the limited generation depth of implanted defects hinder both high-sensitivity sensing and conclusive microscopic identification. Here we engineer high-quality defects by decoupling oxygen incorporation and defect formation, realizing highly homogeneous spin-resonance frequencies as well as narrow optical linewidths and long T2* coherence time. Further, we demonstrate defect formation beyond the ion range utilizing oxygen diffusion, exceptional among impurities in SiC. We further provide hyperfine-interaction statistics of 17O and host nuclei across many PL6 defects, making the oxygen-vacancy origin conclusive. Together, the microscopic identification and the demonstrated formation route establish a foundation for developing the oxygen-vacancy spin defect into a versatile quantum platform.

papers.title: Chaos Made Visible: Active particles trace Lorenz-like attractors in physical space
papers.summary: Chaotic attractors are typically visualized in an abstract phase space. Here we show that an orientable active particle moving through a steady, two-dimensional, multivortex flow can trace a Lorenz-like chaotic attractor in its real space trajectory. Despite the flow being strictly time independent, coupling between particle position and orientation creates a three-dimensional nonlinear dynamical system. For suitable particle shape and swimming speed, the trajectory organizes into a striking two-lobed geometry reminiscent of the classical Lorenz attractor. A structured first return map, positive largest Lyapunov exponent, and a broadband power spectrum establish that the underlying motion is chaotic. Varying the swimming speed reveals a rich sequence of dynamical regimes as self-propulsion breaks streamline confinement and reorganizes the particle motion. Our results demonstrate how an internal orientational degree of freedom can make chaotic dynamics directly visible in physical space, allowing a single active particle to trace a chaotic attractor as it moves through an otherwise steady flow.

papers.title: Residual Expert Routing for Text-Only Domain Adaptation of Factorized Transducer ASR
papers.summary: Fine-tuning the non-blank predictor of a factorized transducer on target-domain text improves recognition on that domain but degrades performance on the source domain. A single interpolation weight between base and adapted predictors cannot resolve this: the adapted predictor helps at some prefixes and hurts at others, often within one utterance. We propose conservative residual routing: the adapted predictor becomes a residual correction to the base, and a 16k-parameter gate decides at each prefix how much of it to admit. Closing the gate reproduces the base exactly. On a 40-hour conversational corpus, routing retains essentially all of the text-only gain on two held-out domains (19.89 to 16.74, 20.91 to 16.21 WER) while leaving source-domain WER unchanged (12.90 to 12.93); the adapted predictor alone costs 1.08 WER. Routing needs no per-domain tuning on target-domain audio. Analysis reveals the gate does not behave as a simple domain-level switch: it modulates intervention through the disagreement between the two predictors, suppressing it in-domain and amplifying it out-of-domain.

papers.title: EditJev: System One Routing for Image Editing Models
papers.summary: Instruction-based image editing models exhibit pronounced sample-specific performance variation: different models can produce substantially different results for the same source image and editing instruction, and the best-performing model often varies across requests. These models also differ substantially in inference latency, making fixed-model deployment inefficient. We therefore study image editing model routing, which dynamically selects an editor from a candidate pool given an input image and editing instruction. We introduce EditJev, a System One routing model that directly predicts sample-level preference scores over candidate image editing models in a single forward pass. A lightweight preference head on a vision-language backbone produces a fixed-dimensional score vector without autoregressive model-name generation or response parsing. To train EditJev, we construct pairwise preferences from offline candidate outputs and optimize a pairwise ranking objective to learn relative model suitability. At inference time, EditJev combines the predicted preference scores with model-level speed scores to balance editing quality and generation latency. Experiments on ImgEdit and GEdit-En show that EditJev improves aggregate quality over the strongest fixed editor, from 4.540 to 4.592 and from 8.194 to 8.255, respectively, while reducing estimated end-to-end latency by 60.8% and 31.7%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of direct, structured model routing for efficient image editing.

papers.title: From Link Availability to Deadline-Constrained Key Service: A Feasibility Framework for Mobile Free-Space Quantum Key Distribution
papers.summary: Mobile free-space quantum key distribution (QKD) links can provide secret bits intermittently, whereas applications may need cryptographic key material at specified times. Optical feasibility, positive finite-key output, and deadline-compliant key service are consequently different claims. This technical note formalizes their separation through a time-indexed, security-qualified arrival process and a key-inventory model. Under explicitly stated assumptions, an elementary prefix-feasibility condition characterizes whether all demands can be served without borrowing keys from future contact windows. A stylized finite block model then illustrates why positive long-run optical availability does not ensure positive finite-key output when observations are fragmented into short contacts. Two transparent numerical examples distinguish total key yield from key delivery time and show the conditional benefit of pooling data across acquisition windows. The analysis is intended as a systems-level accounting and benchmarking framework, not a new QKD security proof or a demonstration of hardware performance. It identifies measurements and security assumptions needed to evaluate train, UAV, high-altitude-platform, and satellite-assisted optical QKD against application-level service requirements.

papers.title: Natural-Language to Nav2: Operational Policies for Costmap-Based Navigation
papers.summary: Autonomous mobile robots support material transport in warehouses and industrial facilities, where navigation must adapt to changing operating conditions. Sensor observations reveal physical obstacles, but do not by themselves specify temporary access rules, route preferences, or exceptions known to operators. This paper presents a natural-language policy interface that brings this knowledge into ROS 2 Nav2. A local large language model converts instructions into JSON policies specifying destinations, spatial constraints, and temporal or event conditions. Deterministic checks govern mission acceptance, and three costmap adapters project accepted policies into the existing navigation stack without changing its planner or controller. On 150 researcher-authored English commands, four local models produce 107-142 correct accepted policies, compared with 44 for a rule-based parser, with 3-20 incorrect acceptances per model. Fault injection records rejection of eight endpoint/JSON faults and 29 validator-stage faults. Navigation experiments use correct task policies to evaluate keepouts, zone costs, person-dependent regions, and event-conditioned passage in simulation and on a TurtleBot3. For Tasks 1-3, mean travel times are 18.4-24.5% lower in simulation and 23.1-35.0% lower on the physical testbed than with the baseline lacking those policies. A native KeepoutFilter comparison and two-robot demonstrations examine basic keepout behavior and shared policy projection. The interface connects operator instructions to explicit navigation policies while retaining Nav2's planning and control components.
papers.comment: 23 pages, 16 figures, including supplementary material. Jiyeong Chae and Hyunkyo Seo contributed equally. Project page: https://a56239637-dot.github.io/Natural-Language-to-Nav2-Project-Page/

papers.title: When does boundary-condition uncertainty outweigh thermal and vegetation effects in street canyon flow? A global sensitivity analysis of input uncertainty
papers.summary: Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) is increasingly used to resolve wind, heat, and pollution patterns in cities with high fidelity but high computational cost. Thermal effects and vegetation are often neglected despite being important drivers, yet their influence may be masked by variability from other uncertain inputs. This work determines how precisely model parameters and boundary conditions must be known for these effects to govern output uncertainty in the velocity, temperature, and concentration fields of a two-dimensional street canyon. A global Sobol analysis of 24 parameters is made tractable by a surrogate trained on Reynolds-Averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) simulations, combining principal component analysis (PCA) with multilayer perceptrons (MLPs). Two ventilation regimes assess the variance due to thermal and vegetation parameters as uncertainty in all other inputs is progressively reduced. At typical uncertainty levels, turbulence closure constants and inflow turbulence profiles govern variability in all three fields in both regimes. Under weak ventilation, solar forcing becomes the main source of temperature variability once the remaining uncertainties are halved, and of concentration variance once they are reduced to a quarter (about $\pm11\%$ for the dominant closure constant and $\pm12\%$ for the emission rate). In contrast, vegetation contributes significantly at typical uncertainty levels. Under strong ventilation, however, the canopy never overtakes the closure constants, even when the dominant one is known to $\pm5\%$. Spatially, both effects peak at road level and along canyon walls, which influence outdoor exposure and indoor infiltration, suggesting that high-resolution exposure studies should account for them.

papers.title: Acquisition for Spherical-Linear Bayesian Optimization on the Cube
papers.summary: Recent work demonstrated that executing Bayesian Optimization (BO) using simply a linear surrogate with a clever transformation is enough to approximate the performance of the standard Gaussian-Process (GP) based version on high-dimensional test functions. When the decision region is a sphere, this strategy admits rapid exact acquisition. However, it is the unit cube we encounter most often in the BO literature, and in this setting a standard approach, namely a multi-start quasi-Newton method, is employed for solving the acquisition subproblem. In this article, we will discuss a series of results, both positive and negative, regarding the complexity of global resolution of various acquisition subproblems over the unit cube. On the basis of this discussion, we will propose a new acquisition function which is globally optimizable using significantly less execution time than the incumbent approach while maintaining or improving performance. The resulting method is competitive with GP-based BO in terms of accuracy per evaluation, and is superior in terms of accuracy per walltime on black-boxes of low to moderate computational intensity.

papers.title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Loss Exploration for Vision-Based Perception under Non-IID Data
papers.summary: Vision-based image classification models benefit from Federated Learning (FL) across vehicles, however learning accurate models from distributed vehicular cameras is challenging due to data heterogeneity and privacy concerns. To improve performance on non-IID data, advanced FL optimization approaches have emerged that share auxiliary insights, such as client gradient behaviors. While these gradient-guided optimized FL methods improve the model accuracy, their reliance on sharing additional gradient information introduces a previously unexplored privacy vulnerability. In our empirical privacy-leakage experiment, we show that a malicious server can infer clients' label sets from shared guidance matrices under heterogeneous client label distributions (simulated via Dirichlet-based label partitions), between 50% and 84% accuracy. To address this privacy leakage, we propose PPFLex that replaces the central server with three Secure Multi-Party Computation (MPC) servers to securely compute the global guidance matrix and perform federated averaging under semi-honest and malicious MPC server assumptions. We evaluate PPFLex on widely used traffic-sign classification datasets (e.g., GTSRB and BTSC) as representative autonomous vehicle perception benchmarks, comparing against baselines. Our results show that PPFLex achieves accuracy comparable to the plain-text FedLEx pipeline while preventing privacy leakage, incurring acceptable MPC overhead.

papers.title: Spatial distribution of star formation in dwarf galaxies: Merger-driven and secular starburst
papers.summary: Galaxy interactions can induce bursts of star formation (SF), while internal or secular processes can also trigger starbursts (SB). Recent studies of the spatial distribution of SF in high-mass (M$_{*}>10^{10}M_{\odot}$) SB galaxies show that SF is centrally concentrated in merger-driven SBs, whereas in secularly driven SB systems, SF is uniformly enhanced across the system. However, it is not clear whether such distinct spatial signatures are present in low-mass (M$_{*} < 10^{10} M_{\odot}$) SB galaxies. In this context, we studied the SF properties of a sample of 272 isolated SB (i.e., with no massive galaxy, within a 1 Mpc$^3$ volume) dwarf galaxies consisting of 17 post-merger and 255 non-interacting SB galaxies, spanning a stellar mass range of $10^{7}-10^{9.6} M_{\odot}$ and a redshift range of 0.01-0.12. For this study, we utilise FUV imaging data from GALEX to estimate the star formation rates of our sample galaxies. We investigated the spatial variation of SB activity by comparing star formation rate surface density (SFRD) across radial bins for post-merger and non-interacting samples of dwarfs. We find an enhancement in SFRD across all radial bins for both samples, and that the enhancement is more or less uniform across the galaxy, within uncertainties. This indicates that SF in low-mass SB galaxies is uniformly enhanced throughout the galaxy, regardless of the mechanism that triggers the SB. This contrasts with observations in massive galaxies, where SF is centrally concentrated in merger-driven SB systems. The lack of central concentration of SF in low-mass merger systems could be due to their shallow gravitational potentials and the compression of extended gaseous envelopes during interactions, which trigger SF across these galaxies. Deeper, higher-spatial-resolution observations are essential for better understanding the spatial distribution of SF in low-mass galaxies.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in A&A, 8 pages, 4 figures

papers.title: Trace-distance characterization of recurrent pairwise synchronization in cavity-coupled superconducting qubits
papers.summary: We theoretically investigate recurrent pairwise synchronization in three super?conducting qubits coupled to a common single-mode microwave cavity. The qubits interact indirectly through the cavity field and are driven by a coher?ent microwave field. We obtain the coherent dynamics in the dressed-state basis and quantify pairwise synchronization by the trace distance between reduced single-qubit density matrices. The trace-distance dynamics exhibit oscillatory wave-packet structures, with low-trace-distance regions identifying finite syn?chronization windows. An envelope-threshold procedure is introduced to extract the representative duration of these windows. By varying the middle-qubit coupling strength and the relative coupling ratio of the outer qubits, we con?struct a parameter-dependent map of the synchronization-window duration. The duration decreases rapidly with increasing relative outer-qubit coupling and becomes weakly dependent on the middle-qubit coupling in the stronger-coupling regime. These results provide a reduced-state-based characterization of coherent collective dynamics in multiqubit circuit-QED systems.
papers.comment: 11 pages, 4 figures. Submitted to Quantum Information Processing

papers.title: A Large-Volume GAGG(Ce) Detector Module for In-Beam $γ$-Ray Spectroscopy
papers.summary: We report on the development and characterization of large-volume GAGG(Ce) scintillation detector modules equipped with silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) readout. Each module houses four large-volume GAGG(Ce) crystals within a compact thin carbon-fiber enclosure, minimizing the passive material budget and enabling the construction of high-efficiency, large-solid-angle detector arrays for in-beam $γ$-ray spectroscopy. The performance of 10 GAGG modules (40 detectors), including the energy linearity, energy and timing resolution, and intrinsic full-energy peak efficiency, was evaluated using standard $γ$-ray sources and $^{14}$N(p,$γ$)$^{15}$O reactions, covering a $γ$-ray energy range from about 0.3 MeV to 8 MeV. Non-linear energy response across the measured energy range was observed due to the non-linear response of the SiPM. The detector modules exhibit good energy resolution (FWHM below 5\% at 1.33 MeV), good timing resolution (FWHM $\sim$500 ps at $\sim$1 MeV), and intrinsic full-energy peak efficiencies in good agreement with Geant4 simulations, making the detector modules a promising solution for next-generation high efficiency in-beam $γ$-ray experiments at RI-beam facilities.

papers.title: What Transfers Across Protein Pockets? Experience Reuse in Molecular Optimization for Agentic Structure-Based Drug Design
papers.summary: LLM agents optimize a ligand in a protein pocket by editing it step by step and docking each edit. Recent agents first spend extra dockings probing the complex with controlled edits; guidance induced from these probes is reported to help more than the chemical knowledge the model already carries. The probes are then discarded with the instance that produced them, so the obvious next step is to keep them in an experience base, letting a new pocket inherit what earlier ones already paid for. Such a base is read through a \emph{key}: the record properties under which past edits are pooled and a new one is looked up. Using the full log of one such run over the CrossDocked2020 test-set pockets, we ask whether its keys recur on a pocket the base has never seen and still separate improving from worsening edits. \crchange{Using} the contacts at the site being edited, the action, and the round as \crchange{a} key, the base separates them sharply. Within our analysis, this separation is largely explained by how much the edit changed the molecule's size, the action, and the round, none of which describes the target. That is not because the target is irrelevant: naming it outright separates them several times more sharply. For a pocket absent from the base, transfer must rely on a description rather than its identity. Among the exact-match descriptions we evaluate, the more specific ones rarely recur, whereas the coarser ones provide little separation; the signals that do transfer primarily describe the edit and the molecule it produced rather than the target. Under the representations and lookup scheme studied here, an experience base may be more useful for prioritizing an agent's own proposals for docking than for directly prescribing what to build.

papers.title: Development of an Analog Front-End Using NINO ASIC for Mini-ICAL
papers.summary: The mini-ICAL was supposed to be a pre-prototype detector of the Iron CALorimeter (ICAL) of the India-based Neutrino Observatory (INO) project. Resistive Plate Chamber (RPC) was the active element of these detectors. As this detector operates in avalanche mode, one needs a very fast pre-amplifier for signal processing. NINO ASIC developed for the ALICE time-of-flight detector was a potential chip to be used as the analog-front end. This paper presents an 8-in-1 pre-amplifier board developed using the NINO ASIC, a single-ended to differential signal conversion using the differential driver chip manufactured by Texas Instruments, production of the boards, lessons learned during production, testing of these boards, and interface with RPCs. Finally, its performance based on strip rates and efficiency of the detector will also be discussed.

papers.title: Earth embeddings are decomposable records of the land surface
papers.summary: Ecological monitoring, carbon accounting and biodiversity assessment increasingly rely on annual Earth embeddings--learned vectors that compress a year of satellite observation for every ten-meter pixel on Earth, consumed in place of the imagery itself. What these vectors mean has not been established. Here we decompose two widely used embedding products and show that they contain individual ecological features, including fire, forest clearing and crop type, validated against independent reference data on events across six continents. The recovered concepts date abrupt canopy loss to the first post-disturbance growing season and resolve severity well enough to separate prescribed fire from wildfire. Small fires that recover quickly are detectable in one product but not the other, which instead separates crops more strongly.

papers.title: Risk Adequacy and Anti-Discrimination in Insurance Pricing: Classification, Aggregation, and Transfers
papers.summary: Insurance tariffs must reconcile risk-based pricing, portfolio coverage, and anti-discrimination requirements. We introduce a framework in which tariffs are constructed through classification, aggregation of benchmark risk prices within classes, and balanced transfers, and are evaluated by several distinct criteria. This yields a multi-objective tariff-design problem whose attainable objective set and Pareto frontier describe the resulting trade-offs. Risk adequacy is measured by the discrepancy between charged premiums and individual benchmark risk prices. Portfolio coverage is assessed through the capital required to make aggregate claims net of premium income acceptable. Anti-discrimination is examined through differences in protected-group composition across tariff classes and through premium effects experienced by protected groups. We analyze the trade-offs among these criteria and prove mathematical results characterizing their relationships: (i) the inferential threshold for perfect risk adequacy with finitely many benchmark-price levels; (ii) lower bounds on risk inadequacy under stricter inferential constraints; (iii) exact changes in risk inadequacy and inferential disparity when classes are merged, and dynamic programming for scalarized optimization over consecutive benchmark-price classes; (iv) attainable protected-group total premium effects and their minimum risk inadequacy costs under balanced transfers; (v) a sharp lower bound linking inferential disparity to the risk inadequacy required under a bound on protected-group premium-effect dispersion; and (vi) conditions for portfolio-coverage improvement and its additional risk inadequacy cost at fixed protected-group total premium effects. A numerical motor-insurance study illustrates the results.

papers.title: Optimizing Quantum Battery via Counterdiabatic driving
papers.summary: We analyze the energy charging of a quantum battery within an open quantum framework, where the interaction between the battery element and an external power source is mediated by an ancilla system acting as a controllable switch. Specifically, we investigate the charging and discharging dynamics of a cavity-based quantum battery coupled to a driven qubit functioning as the charger. To ensure lossless power transfer, we utilize an adiabatic evolution protocol. Furthermore, we implement counterdiabatic driving, achieved by applying an auxiliary control field to the original Hamiltonian, to suppress undesired transitions and realize fast adiabatic dynamics. This scheme significantly accelerates the charging process. We demonstrate that the charging efficiency under adiabatic evolution is enhanced and exhibits stable, non-oscillatory behavior, and we determine the optimal duration for the operation. Finally, we show that counterdiabatic driving minimizes the path length between the initial and final states, inducing the shortest possible evolution distance.

papers.title: Channel orthogonalization via movable antennas
papers.summary: This paper investigates the orthogonalization of far-field multiuser channels through the optimal positioning of the antennas constituting an array. To solve the ensuing continuous geometry optimization problem, a graph-theoretic framework is introduced that maps pairwise user channel correlations to graph edges, translating channel orthogonalization into a discrete graph-covering problem on a complete graph. The minimum number of array antennas required for orthogonalization is established for 1D, 2D, and 3D array geometries, and a binary linear program is formulated that identifies the most compact array attaining such orthogonality. The graph framework is also shown to accommodate null-steering scenarios and multipath channels. Furthermore, a fundamental tradeoff is revealed whereby relaxing exact orthogonality to near-orthogonality reduces the antenna count at the expense of a less compact array, and a method is presented to enforce minimum antenna spacings without sacrificing orthogonality.

papers.title: QuantumBilliards.jl: An extensible, user friendly, high-performance Julia library for the large scale computation of spectra and eigenstates of quantum billiards and related problems
papers.summary: We present QuantumBilliards.jl, an open-source Julia library providing a suite of numerical solvers for the two-dimensional interior Helmholtz eigenproblem with Dirichlet boundary conditions, a paradigmatic model in quantum chaos. The library implements conventional wavenumber-sweep techniques together with several accelerated eigensolvers: the Vergini--Saraceno scaling method, the expanded boundary integral method (EBIM), Beyn's contour-integral method, and the Compact Rational Krylov (CORK) method. It provides a common framework for constructing billiard geometries, exploiting discrete symmetries, computing eigenvalues and eigenstates, and treating smooth, cornered, and multiply connected domains. The library further includes reconstruction of eigenfunctions from boundary normal derivatives and the computation of Poincaré--Husimi (PH) phase-space representations. Available at: https://github.com/Quantum-Chaos-Julia/QuantumBilliards.jl.

papers.title: Let's Do Turbulence Right: In Space and Time!
papers.summary: The three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations govern fluid turbulence, a chaotic and non-linear physical phenomenon characterized by complex eddies interacting across vast spatial and temporal scales. A numerically accurate modeling of this multi-scale energy cascade requires fully resolving both the fine spatial structures and the continuous temporal evolution of the flow field. In this paper, we leverage massive, time-resolved direct numerical simulations, which exceed 28 TB per run, to assess how numerical choices govern the resolved (3+1)-dimensional physics of turbulent flows. Building on this analysis, we study how neural networks represent the recorded turbulent motion. Our results highlight that spatial and temporal assessments can disagree for both numerical records and learned representations. We therefore call on the machine learning community to treat (3+1)-dimensional turbulence as a four-dimensional phenomenon.

papers.title: New time-periodic solutions to the cubic conformal wave equation on $\mathbb{S}^{3}$: I Spherical symmetry
papers.summary: We present a rigorous construction of novel time-periodic solutions to the radially symmetric cubic conformal wave equation on the Einstein cylinder $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{S}^{3}$. Their existence, hinted by the earlier numerical studies (arXiv:2504.10513), complements prior results on Cantor sets of infinitesimally small solutions. Our proof, based on the contraction principle, requires extensive computations that are performed on a computer by the means of rational arithmetic. We are able to significantly reduce their amount by a thorough analysis of the inverse of the associated linear operator, leading to sharper analytical bounds, as well as introduction of simplified versions of certain relevant operators. We provide examples of three solutions with specific frequency; however, our techniques and tools can be directly adapted to prove the existence of other solutions conjectured in (arXiv:2504.10513).
papers.comment: 23 pages, 2 figures; supplementary material (Mathematica code and data files) is available at https://github.com/mmal/conformal-wave-cap

papers.title: Gauge-field energy density in inflationary kinetic-coupling models: QFT regularization versus horizon cutoffs
papers.summary: Coupling gauge fields to the inflaton can amplify their quantum fluctuations during inflation, with potential applications to a range of cosmological phenomena. A central challenge is to define finite and physically meaningful observables, such as the gauge-field energy density. In this work, we study an Abelian gauge field kinetically coupled to the inflaton through $f^2(φ)F_{μν}F^{μν}$ in a de Sitter background with $f\propto a^{γ_1}$, and compare conventional quantum-field-theoretic regularization with horizon-cutoff prescriptions. Using a hard physical-momentum cutoff and dimensional regularization, we derive the ultraviolet divergences in closed form and fix the remaining one-parameter finite-part ambiguity by requiring the coupling-induced total energy density to be nonnegative. We then examine five horizon-cutoff prescriptions based on characteristic scales of the mode equations. Their predictions depend sensitively on the choice of horizon scale and, for weak gauge-field production, can deviate substantially from the regularized result; for the adopted finite-part prescription, the minimal horizon agrees best with the regularized total energy density. As $|γ_1|\to 2$, where infrared modes dominate, the relative deviation of all prescriptions from the regularized result vanishes, independently of the finite-part prescription. Outside this regime, the separate electric and magnetic contributions, which can become negative after regularization, are not reliably reproduced by any of the horizon-cutoff prescriptions.

papers.title: OWLS: Open-world Language-conditioned Speed Fields for Zero-Shot Rover Navigation
papers.summary: Semantics can provide a proxy for physical traversability. Terrain that looks like loose sand or a rock field is likely to have similar physical properties. Open-vocabulary vision-language models (VLMs) enable this physical reasoning over terrain outside any fixed label set. We present Open-world Language-conditioned Speed Fields (OWLS), which plans directly over the dense feature map of a VLM. Prompted with a description of traversable terrain, the VLM scores every pixel of a single camera image; OWLS projects these scores onto the ground, adapts them to the platform with two morphological operations, and uses the result as the speed field of a minimum-time planner, so terrain appearance and obstacle clearance shape one trajectory. OWLS needs no task-specific training, no terrain annotation, no persistent map, and no exteroceptive sensor beyond the camera. We evaluate it on a physical rover indoors and off-road, on simulated Mars and Moon rovers over 200 procedurally generated terrains, and on real planetary imagery.

papers.title: The Compendium of Super-Quadratic Computational Quantum Advantages
papers.summary: This compendium presents a structured collection of computational problems with credible prospects for realizing meaningful quantum advantage, focused on describing problem characteristics rather than specific algorithms. It is intended for non-quantum researchers and practitioners with strong computational backgrounds, particularly domain experts, seeking to assess the relevance of quantum methods to real-world problems. The compendium focuses on enumerating core problems for which there is good evidence that a quantum computer can realize more than a quadratic speedup in offline non-relativized time-complexity (e.g., as opposed to in oracular settings, streaming models, or communication advantages). Entries characterize the structural constraints that real-world instances must satisfy to realize those advantages in practice. The intention is to provide a reference that can be leveraged to connect quantum algorithms to practical use cases.

papers.title: Political sense-making in "individual" human-technology-world relations: the case of LLM-generated autobiographies
papers.summary: As AI systems increasingly mediate how people describe, recognize, and present themselves, their politics cannot be reduced to what remains hidden inside the "black box." This chapter argues that AI's political significance emerges within technologically, intersubjectively, and temporally mediated interpretive practices. Bringing Arendt's political philosophy into conversation with Gadamerian hermeneutics, the chapter develops a postphenomenological relational-temporal account of political sense-making across Human-Technology-World relations. Against the charge that postphenomenology remains individualistic and using the case of LLM-generated biographies, the chapter shows how seemingly private human-LLM encounters are worldly and collective. When users ask systems such as ChatGPT to describe them, they do not simply receive algorithmic representations. They interpret, contest, edit, share, and publicly test these descriptions. In doing so, people move interpretively among affective resonance, friction, public re-articulation, and the sedimentation of meaning. This means that the so-called "micro-level" of postphenomenological analysis is already saturated with publicity: affective uptake becomes communicable, reflection becomes accountable, and uses sediment into shared standards of appearance.
